brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetic characteristics of KC1086 in combination with fulvestrant in adults with hormone receptor-positive (HR+), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
conditions: HR-positive, HER2-negative Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer
title: KC1086 in Combination With Fulvestrant for HR-Positive, HER2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
This study is testing two doses of imetelstat in adults with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome, or MDS. The study will include about 100 adults in several countries. To be eligible, participants must have lower-risk MDS, need frequent red blood cell transfusions, and have already tried-or cannot use-other treatments for anemia. Participants will be randomly placed into one of two groups. One group will receive the usual dose of imetelstat, 7.1 mg/kg of body weight. The other group will receive a lower dose, 3.55 mg/kg. Both doses are given through a vein during a roughly two-hour clinic visit every four weeks. Participants won't be told which dose they receive, but their study doctors and the study sponsor will know.

The main goal is to learn whether the lower dose can be safer while still reducing transfusion needs.

Blood tests will be done often, especially early in treatment. If blood counts fall too much or other serious side effects occur, treatment may be delayed, lowered, or stopped. Participants in the lower-dose group who have no clear benefit after at least six treatment cycles may be allowed to move to the higher dose if they meet safety requirements. Study treatment can continue until the disease gets worse, side effects become too severe, patient chooses to stop, or the study ends. Study visits include blood tests, physical exams, vital signs, reviews of transfusions and side effects, and sometimes cardiac or bone marrow tests. Investigators will also collect extra blood samples to study imetelstat pharmacokinetic and how it affects blood cells and MDS-related genes.

Taking part is voluntary. Participants may leave the study at any time.
primary_outcomes: Rate of ≥ 12-week Red Blood Cell Transfusion Independence (RBC TI) with concurrent mean Hgb rise of at least 1.5 g/dL
Rate of Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia by laboratory values
title: A Trial Evaluating Two Imetelstat Doses in Participants With Lower Risk Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS)

brief_summary: This is a single center, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of MAX-001 in participants with post-operative dental pain after wisdom teeth removal.
primary_outcomes: Summed Pain Intensity Difference 12 hours (SPID12) vs placebo using the Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) for pain
Incidence of Treatment Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) as assessed by patient response to questions and spontaneous reporting of TEAEs

brief_summary:
Spinal anesthesia is widely used for surgical procedures involving the lower body. Accurate determination of sensory block height is important for ensuring adequate anesthesia and patient safety. Sensory block levels are conventionally assessed using clinical tests that depend on patient responses.

Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a noninvasive monitoring technique that measures regional tissue oxygen saturation (StO₂). Changes in tissue oxygenation following spinal anesthesia may reflect alterations in regional perfusion associated with sympathetic blockade.

This prospective observational study primarily aims to evaluate whether segmental NIRS measurements at the T10 dermatomal level can objectively identify the achievement of a sensory block reaching T10 or higher, a clinically relevant threshold for selected surgical procedures.

As a secondary objective, NIRS measurements at the T4 level will be evaluated to investigate whether changes in regional tissue oxygenation reflect further cephalad spread of spinal anesthesia.

Regional tissue oxygen saturation will be monitored at T10 and T4 before and after spinal anesthesia. NIRS-derived parameters will be compared with clinically determined sensory block levels.

The study will also investigate relationships between segmental NIRS changes, sensory block progression, and hemodynamic alterations.

The findings may contribute to the development of an objective, noninvasive method for monitoring the extent of spinal anesthesia.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy of T10 NIRS at 5 Minutes After Spinal Anesthesia
title: Monitoring Spinal Anesthesia Block Level Using Segmental Near-Infrared Spectroscopy

brief_summary:
Purpose of This Observational Study

This study aims to understand the real-world effectiveness of furmonertinib for patients with stage IA2 (high-risk) to IB, EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have undergone curative surgical resection and carry high risk factors for recurrence, and to evaluate the safety of the drug in this population. It is designed to answer the following key questions:

What is the 3-year disease-free survival rate for these early-stage lung cancer patients who take furmonertinib after surgery? What potential health issues may participants experience while taking furmonertinib? What are the 2-year and 3-year overall survival rates, and overall disease-free survival outcomes for patients taking furmonertinib after surgery? This study will not change participants' regular clinical treatment plans. We will only observe and record treatment and follow-up data of patients receiving furmonertinib adjuvant therapy in real clinical settings. The furmonertinib dosage is 80mg taken orally once daily, treatment duration follows actual clinical arrangements, and the core observation period is 3 years.
conditions: Early Stage Lung Non-Small Cell Carcinoma
lead_sponsor: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
title: Study of Furmonertinib as Follow-Up Treatment After Surgery for Early-Stage EGFR-Positive Lung Cancer: Real-World Observation

brief_summary: This study will enroll older adults with sarcopenia (Spleen-Kidney Deficiency Pattern) who will receive exercise and nutritional interventions. By assessing changes from baseline in DXA-measured appendicular muscle mass and other efficacy outcomes, the study aims to characterize the longitudinal changes in sarcopenia over a 24-week period and provide an external control for a future randomized, double-blind clinical trial of Peiyuan Guben Tongluo Ointment in older adults with sarcopenia (Spleen-Kidney Deficiency Pattern).
title: Exercise and Nutritional Intervention in Older Adults With Sarcopenia (Spleen-Kidney Deficiency Pattern)

brief_summary: This pilot study will evaluate the safety and tolerability of Filsuvez, a topical gel, in newborns and infants younger than 6 months with dystrophic or junctional epidermolysis bullosa. Filsuvez is approved for patients 6 months of age and older but has not been studied in this younger population. Participants will receive Filsuvez for 180 days and will be followed with clinical assessments, laboratory testing, caregiver questionnaires, telephone contacts, and standardized photographs. The study will also explore changes in wound size, disease activity, pain, and family burden during and after treatment.
primary_outcomes: the safety and tolerability of Filsuvez
title: Filsuvez in Infants With Dystrophic or Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa

brief_summary:
Severe pneumonia is a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children and often requires hospitalization and prolonged medical care. Vitamin D plays an important role in immune regulation and inflammatory responses, and its supplementation may help improve outcomes in respiratory infections. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness in reducing the duration of hospital stay among children with severe pneumonia remains limited.

This randomized controlled trial will be conducted at the Department of Pediatrics, Divisional Headquarters Teaching Hospital, Mirpur, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, over six months after approval of the synopsis. A total of 114 children of either sex, aged 1-16 years, presenting with severe pneumonia will be enrolled through non-probability consecutive sampling. Patients with a history of tuberculosis, congenital heart disease, cleft lip or palate, bronchial asthma, upper airway abnormality, urinary tract infection, malaria, dengue, typhoid fever, or malnourishment will be excluded.

Eligible participants will be randomly allocated into two groups using sealed opaque envelopes. Group A will receive a single oral dose of 200,000 IU vitamin D3 dissolved in 10 mL of peanut oil, while Group B will receive 10 mL of peanut oil as placebo. Both preparations will be identical in color, taste, smell, consistency, and container. Participants will be followed until discharge. Hospital length of stay, defined as the period from admission to discharge, will be recorded for each patient. Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 20. Mean hospital length of stay will be compared between the two groups using an independent samples t-test, with p≤0.05 considered statistically significant.

The study aims to determine whether a single high dose of vitamin D3 reduces hospital length of stay compared with placebo in children presenting with severe pneumonia.
lead_sponsor: Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Institue of Trauma
title: Effect of Single High-Dose Vitamin D3 Versus Placebo on Hospital Length of Stay in Children With Severe Pneumonia.

brief_summary:
This study compared three treatments for myofascial pain in adults with clinical features of bruxism, such as tooth clenching or grinding. Myofascial pain is pain arising from muscles and sensitive areas within them.

Ninety adults aged 18-60 years were randomly assigned to one of three groups: dry needling, botulinum toxin type A injections, or an occlusal splint worn at night together with medication. Dry needling involved inserting thin needles into sensitive points in the masseter muscles. Botulinum toxin injections were administered into the masseter muscles on both sides. The splint group received tizanidine and paracetamol for one month.

The study assessed pain at rest and during jaw function, sensitivity to pressure, and mouth opening. Assessments were performed before treatment and at one day, one week, and one month after treatment. The purpose was to compare the short-term effects of these three treatments.
conditions: Myofascial Pain - Dysfunction Syndrome of TMJ
title: Comparison of Three Treatments for Myofascial Pain in Patients With Bruxism

brief_summary: This study tests whether an artificial intelligence (AI) system that drafts tumor board recommendations performs as well on new cases as it did on archived cases. The system runs in shadow mode at three multidisciplinary tumor boards of TUM University Hospital rechts der Isar. For each case it drafts a recommendation before the board meets. The board does not see the draft, and the draft has no influence on patient care. After the meeting, each draft is compared with the board decision. The agreement rate is then compared with the rate measured on archived decisions of the same boards.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Cases With Category Match Between System Draft and Board Decision
title: Shadow-Mode Evaluation of an AI Assistant for Multidisciplinary Tumor Boards

brief_summary: CMT-PROFILE is a single-center, cross-sectional observational study involving adults with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT). The study will investigate the association between clinical disease severity, measured using the CMT Examination Score version 2 (CMTES-v2), and motor electrophysiological parameters, including compound muscle action potential (CMAP) amplitudes and motor nerve conduction velocities. Secondary objectives include characterizing clinical-electrophysiological concordance, comparing functional capacity, muscle strength and mobility across concordance groups, and exploring demographic, clinical, biological and genetic factors associated with variability in disease expression. Approximately 250 patients are planned for inclusion. All assessments will be performed at a single reference time point (M0), with no longitudinal follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Association Between CMTES-v2 and Motor Electrophysiological Parameters
title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Heterogeneity in Adult Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease

brief_summary:

The study comprises of a screening and treatment period using the conjunctival allergen challenge model to evaluate TL-925 for the treatment of allergic conjunctivitis.

brief_summary:
Checkpoint+ is a community-based observational study designed to better understand barriers to HIV prevention, early diagnosis, and sexual health care among migrant men who have sex with men, trans people, and non-binary people. The study collects information on participants' migration experiences, access to health services, perceived barriers, and suggestions for improving culturally appropriate and accessible HIV and sexual health services.

Based on the proposals made by the community, a set of community-based interventions will be selected and implemented to encourage more migrant MSM, trans and non-binary people to access BCN Checkpoint for the first time for HIV testing and other sexual health services. The interventions will then be evaluated, and the most successful ones will be implemented again to maximise their impact.
primary_outcomes: Perceived barriers to HIV testing and sexual health service access
Community proposals for improving access to HIV prevention and early diagnosis
title: Checkpoint+: Improving Access to HIV Prevention and Early Diagnosis Among Migrant Men Who Have Sex With Men, Trans People, and Non-binary People

brief_summary:
This study aims to examine the effectiveness of MIT during the immobilization phase following upper limb injury.

This study adopts a quasi-experimental parallel-group design. Participants will be allocated to either the motor imagery training group or the control group. The motor imagery training group will receive a structured motor imagery training program during the immobilization period, whereas the control group will receive standard patient education on wound and immobilization device care.

The effects of motor imagery training and standard patient education will be compared in terms of sensorimotor cortical engagement, measured by electroencephalography mu-band event-related desynchronization, and hand motor outcomes.
title: Motor Imagery Training During Immobilization for Upper Limb Injury

brief_summary:
This is an open-label, multicenter, Phase II clinical study designed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of HLX22 in combination with serplulimab and either trastuzumab or pertuzumab in patients with HER2-low advanced gastrointestinal cancers.

The study will enroll approximately 128 adults with advanced unresectable colorectal cancer, gastric cancer (including gastroesophageal junction cancer), or biliary tract cancer who have experienced treatment failure after at least two prior lines of standard therapy.

Participants will receive HLX22, serplulimab, and either trastuzumab or pertuzumab by intravenous infusion every three weeks. The primary objective is to evaluate progression-free survival (PFS), which measures how long patients live without their cancer worsening. The study will also assess tumor response, overall survival, and treatment-related side effects.
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
title: HLX22 Plus Serplulimab and Trastuzumab or Pertuzumab in HER2-Low Advanced Gastrointestinal Cancers

brief_summary: This study aims to develop and test the feasibility, as well as the short-term and long-term effectiveness of the tablet-based visual-motor integration training system for preschool children with ASD. It has four key objectives: (1) to develop the tablet-based visual-motor integration training system; (2) to assess whether preschool children with ASD show improvements in visual-motor integration after using the system; (3) to compare the effects of the tablet-based visual-motor integration training system with those of a play-based social interaction group program. In the first year, we recruit five children with ASD. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test are used to compare differences in manual dexterity, visual-motor integration, ocular-motor control, executive function, and adaptive functioning. In the second year, we recruit 15 children with ASD. We examine differences in manual dexterity, visual-motor integration, ocular-motor control, executive function, adaptive behavior, and pretend play performance using paired t-tests. Based on the results from the first and second years, we optimize the tablet-based visual-motor integration training system. In the third year, we recruit a sample of 40 preschool children with ASD, aged 3 to 5 years. These children are randomly assigned to treatment and control groups. The treatment group undergoes 16 weeks of tablet-based visual-motor integration training, while the control group participates in a 16-week play-based social interaction program. Both groups receive a total of 960 minutes of treatment. A Repeated Measures ANOVA are conducted to compare pre- and post-test differences between the treatment and control groups. The findings of this study will be valuable for occupational therapists and clinicians in assisting caregivers with the implementation of the intervention program. Additionally, it will contribute to the body of knowledge regarding the effectiveness of the tablet-based visual-motor integration training system in enhancing the visual-motor integration abilities of preschool children with ASD in Taiwan. Practitioners will be able to use the standard treatment manual to effectively implement the tablet-based training. We expect that the results will enable clinicians to apply empirical knowledge to improve visual-motor integration abilities, ultimately promoting the health and development of preschool children with ASD.
interventions: a tablet-based visual-motor integration training system
primary_outcomes: Developmental Test of Visual Perception, Third Edition (DTVP-3)
Bruininks-Oseretsky Test of Motor Proficiency-Second Edition (BOT-2)
title: Efficacy of Using Tablet as a Tool Visual-Motor Integration Training for Preschool Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder

brief_summary:
This study aims to develop and test a brief tool called the Breakthrough Cancer Pain Assessment (BCPA) for use with cancer patients in Taiwan. The tool is intended to help medical staff assess episodes of breakthrough cancer pain in busy clinical settings.

The study has three stages. First, 14 clinical experts will review an initial set of 11 questions and assess whether they are relevant and important. Second, two medical staff members will separately interview each of 30 patients within three hours on the same day and independently record the answers to evaluate agreement between their ratings. Third, the tool will be applied in 1,043 patients recruited from multiple hospitals who are receiving short-acting opioids other than Painkyl.

In the clinical application stage, physicians will prescribe and individually adjust fentanyl buccal soluble film (Painkyl) for patients whose breakthrough pain is not meaningfully relieved within 15 minutes or whose medication administration route needs adjustment. These patients will be reassessed with the BCPA one to two weeks later. Patients with satisfactory pain relief at the initial assessment will undergo no further study procedures.

The main objectives are to evaluate the content validity and inter-rater reliability of the BCPA. A secondary objective is to determine the percentage of patients reporting meaningful pain relief within or at 15 minutes after taking Painkyl.

The planned secondary assessments also compare the pretreatment and post-treatment percentages of patients reporting meaningful pain relief within 15 minutes and their usual breakthrough pain intensity. Relief is reported by the patient using BCPA item 9; pain intensity is assessed using BCPA item 6 on a 0-to-10 scale.
primary_outcomes: Item-Level Content Validity Index of the BCPA
Scale-Level Content Validity Indices of the BCPA
Inter-Rater Agreement for Categorical BCPA Items
Inter-Rater Consistency for Continuous BCPA Items
title: Development and Testing of a Brief Tool to Assess Breakthrough Cancer Pain in Taiwan

brief_summary:
This study will assess the safety of JULÄINE™, an injectable filler containing poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA), and whether it can improve loose skin on the neck.

The main question is whether more than 60% of treated participants show an improvement of at least one level on a neck skin laxity scale, 26 weeks after their final treatment. Improvement will be measured by comparing neck skin looseness before and after treatment.

The study plans to enroll adults aged 18 years or older with mild to moderately severe loose neck skin at three sites. All participants will receive the filler during three treatment sessions, approximately four weeks apart.

Participation will last approximately 14 months, including screening, treatment, and follow-up until 52 weeks after the final treatment. Investigators will assess changes using standardised photographs, measurements of skin elasticity, and questionnaires about participants' views of their neck appearance. The study will also monitor adverse events through the final follow-up visit.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Improved Neck Skin Laxity
title: JULÄINE™ - Neck Skin Laxity Clinical Investigation

brief_summary:
Overweight and obesity are characterized by excessive or abnormal adiposity and are associated with an increased risk of metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and several chronic diseases. While overweight is not classified as a disease in itself, it represents an early stage in the continuum of excess adiposity and is associated with an increased risk of progression to obesity and the development of obesity-related metabolic complications. Therefore, early intervention during the overweight stage may represent a critical opportunity to prevent or delay disease progression to obesity. Increasing evidence indicates that the gut microbiome plays an important role in metabolic homeostasis and may contribute to the development and progression of overweight and obesity through interactions with host metabolism, intestinal barrier function, immune responses, and microbial-derived metabolites.

This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial will evaluate whether daily supplementation with a chemically characterized wild thyme (Thymus serpyllum L.) extract for 12 weeks can improve body weight and obesity- and overweight-related anthropometric, metabolic, and inflammatory parameters and modulate the gut microbiome in adults with overweight or obesity. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either wild thyme extract or a matching placebo. The primary objective is to evaluate the effect of the intervention on change in body weight after 12 weeks of treatment. Secondary objectives include evaluating changes in body composition, waist circumference, metabolic parameters, inflammatory biomarkers, and intestinal microbiome composition. The study will also investigate whether baseline gut microbiome characteristics or changes in the gut microbiome are associated with the clinical response to treatment, with the aim of identifying potential microbiome-based biomarkers of response. By targeting individuals across the spectrum from overweight to obesity, this study aims to explore whether early intervention in excess adiposity may provide an opportunity to improve metabolic health and potentially reduce progression toward more severe obesity and associated complications.
lead_sponsor: Fundación Pública Andaluza para la Investigación Biomédica Andalucía Oriental
primary_outcomes: Change in body mass index (BMI) from baseline to week 12.
title: Effects of Wild Thyme Extract on Overweight and Obesity

brief_summary:
Uveitis is a group of eye diseases that cause inflammation and may lead to vision loss. The biological processes responsible for these diseases are not fully understood, particularly in rare forms of uveitis.

The purpose of UVEOMICS is to collect and store biological samples and clinical information from adults with infectious or non-infectious uveitis, including rare inflammatory eye diseases known as white dot syndromes. Researchers will study these samples to better understand the causes of eye inflammation and identify biological markers that may help improve diagnosis, monitor disease activity, predict relapses, and guide future treatments.

The study plans to enroll approximately 2,000 adults, including 1,500 patients with uveitis and 500 individuals undergoing cataract surgery who will serve as a comparison group.

Participants may provide blood samples and small samples of fluid from inside the eye (aqueous humor or vitreous fluid), when appropriate. Samples and clinical information may be collected at different stages of the disease and during follow-up visits. Biological samples will be stored for future research and analyzed together with clinical findings and eye imaging results.

This is an observational study. Participation will not change the medical care or treatment participants receive.
primary_outcomes: Number of biological samples collected and stored in the UVEOMICS biobank
title: Collection and Storage of Biological Samples From Patients Affected by Uveitis for Immunological and Multi-omic Studies

brief_summary:
This observational study evaluates the implementation of the epCertify system with the Hiperdia Care Pathway in Primary Health Care, measuring its impact on the clinical control of hypertension and diabetes and on the quality of care records. Systemic arterial hypertension and diabetes mellitus are among the main public health problems in Brazil, due to their high prevalence, chronic nature, and contribution to outcomes such as stroke, renal failure, myocardial infarction, and non-traumatic amputations. In 2021, 26.3% of the Brazilian adult population reported a medical diagnosis of hypertension and about 20 million Brazilians were living with diabetes. In the second four-month period of 2021, only 43.7% of registered hypertensive patients and 46.2% of registered diabetic patients were followed up with a consultation in the last 12 months, which suggests a structural weakness in current care models. epCertify is an integrated digital solution aimed at the longitudinal monitoring of these conditions in PHC. It operates as cloud-based middleware that consolidates and qualifies existing databases (Citizen's Electronic Health Record, e-SUS Atenção Básica, and the National Registry of Health Establishments) and includes automated validation of registrations based on CPF and clinical criteria, real-time monitoring dashboards with alerts for blood pressure control and glycated hemoglobin requests, integration with e-SUS and RNDS, and team training. The system was previously deployed in the participating municipalities under the Juntos pela Saúde project, an initiative of BNDES in partnership with UMANE and managed by IDIS, through technical-scientific cooperation agreements with Instituto epHealth. The deployment involved registration validation, activation of digital tools, team training, and the start of use in clinical routine, and was completed at the time this evaluation began. This is a mixed-methods, observational study, with a retrospective and prospective approach, conducted in 10 Brazilian municipalities in the states of Rio Grande do Norte, Bahia, Maranhão, Paraíba, and Pernambuco, with an estimated population of 220,649 inhabitants, of whom about 158,867 are 18 years of age or older. The analysis follows the RE-AIM framework (reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance) and uses anonymized secondary data from integrated clinical and administrative databases. Eligible participants are adults aged 18 years or older, with an active registration in the epCertify system, residing in the participating municipalities, and with a diagnosis of hypertension (ICD-10 I10-I15) and/or diabetes mellitus (ICD-10 E10-E14) recorded in PEC or identified via a community health worker. Individuals with insufficient clinical data for analysis are excluded. The study adopts a census-based analysis approach, covering all eligible individuals in the databases of the participating municipalities, estimated at between 32,000 and 40,000.

The primary outcomes are blood pressure measurement in Hiperdia patients and glycated hemoglobin requests. The secondary outcomes include good care practice scores for people with hypertension and with diabetes, blood pressure measurement in hypertensive and in diabetic patients, blood pressure control, glycemic control, medical consultations, prescription of antihypertensive and antidiabetic drugs, weight and height measurement, diabetic foot examination, and home visits by community health workers.

The observation period after system deployment is 6 months, compared with the period prior to deployment. The hypothesis is that the implementation of epCertify significantly increases the proportion of patients with up-to-date blood pressure and glycated hemoglobin records relative to the prior period. The methodological approach is a before-and-after design, with the individual as the main unit of analysis and aggregations by municipality or basic health unit. Paired comparison tests, univariate and multivariate logistic regression, and hierarchical mixed-effects models with repeated measures are planned, as well as subgroup analyses and analyses of agreement between community health worker records and the electronic health record using Cohen's Kappa. All data come from routine databases and undergo de-identification before any analysis, with removal of direct identifiers, anonymization through irreversible hashing, and storage in a dedicated cloud instance with restricted access and audit logging. The protocol provides for a request for waiver of the individual Informed Consent Form, based on the logistical unfeasibility of obtaining consent, the absence of risk to individuals, and the exclusive use of anonymized data, with institutional authorization through a Technical Cooperation Agreement executed by the local health authority.
primary_outcomes: Blood pressure measurement among Hiperdia patients
HbA1c test ordering among patients with diabetes
title: epCertify With the Hiperdia Care Pathway

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if electroacupuncture combined with functional resistance training works better than functional resistance training alone for improving early recovery after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction in male military personnel. It will also learn about the safety of this combined therapy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the combined therapy reduce pain and lower blood markers of inflammation (such as CRP and TNF-α) more effectively than exercise alone? Does the combined therapy improve knee function, muscle strength, and balance better than exercise alone? Researchers will compare the combined therapy group (FRT plus electroacupuncture) to the exercise-alone group (FRT only) to see if the combined therapy provides greater benefits.

Participants will:

Receive either functional resistance training alone or functional resistance training combined with electroacupuncture for 4 weeks.

Visit the clinic 5 times a week for their assigned therapy sessions. Undergo assessments before and after the 4-week intervention, including pain questionnaires, knee function tests, muscle strength tests, balance tests, and blood draws.
lead_sponsor: Air Force Military Medical University, China
title: Electroacupuncture Combined Functional Resistance Training Induces Greater Improvements in Functional Rehabilitation

brief_summary: Chronic urticaria (CU) is a dermatological condition characterized by recurrent itchy wheals and/or angioedema persisting for more than six weeks. Despite affecting approximately 1% of the global population, the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying CU remain poorly understood, and current treatment options are limited. We will investigate the proteome of CU by analyzing skin biopsies from patients using mass spectrometry-based proteomics. This approach will enhance our understanding of CU at the molecular level, potentially leading to improved diagnostic tools and more effective targeted therapies, ultimately improving the quality of life for patients suffering from this debilitating condition.
title: The Proteome of Chronic Urticaria

brief_summary: A number of 2570 patients scheduled for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with de novo large coronary vessel lesions (reference vessel diameter ≧2.75 mm) suitable for DCB implantation are openly randomized 1:1 to either intracoronary imaging guidance or angiographic guidance groups. The primary objective is to determine whether the IVUS/OCT-guided DCB strategy reduces the incidence of target vessel failure (TVF) at 12 months compared with the coronary angiography (CAG)-guided strategy.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
title: Strategy of Intracoronary Imaging Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Therapy for De Novo Lesions in Large Coronary Vessels

brief_summary:
The goal of this pre-post randomized controlled experimental trial is to examine the impact of ankle joint manipulation on chronic ankle sprain with a compressed ankle joint in athletes (identified in the proposal as volleyball, basketball, and tennis players) aged 16 to 45 years of both genders.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does ankle joint manipulation effectively reduce pain and improve functional status? Does the treatment successfully increase ankle range of motion (ROM)?

Researchers will compare an experimental group receiving manipulation to a control group receiving no treatment to determine the intervention's effectiveness.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned into two equal groups of 30 patients each.
* Either receive a one-shot manipulation of the head of the fibula or receive no treatment.
* Have their ankle range of motion measured using an electronic goniometer.
* Report their ankle pain levels measured by a numeric analog scale.
* Complete a functional assessment evaluated by the ankle joint functional index.
interventions: Ankle joint manipulation (Head of fibula manipulation)
primary_outcomes: Ankle range of motion measured by an electronic goniometer
title: Effect of Ankle Joint Manipulation on Chronic Ankle Sprain With Compressed Ankle Joint for Volleyball and Basketball Players

brief_summary:
The goal of this pre-post randomized controlled experimental trial is to examine the effect of fibular head mobilization and manipulation on knee pain, stiffness, and range of motion (ROM) in patients with knee osteoarthritis. The study focuses on 40 participants of both genders, ranging in age from 25 to 65 years.

Main Questions

* Does fibular head mobilization improve knee pain and range of motion in patients with knee osteoarthritis?
* What is the impact of fibular head mobilization on knee stiffness and joint function?

Study Design and Comparison

Researchers will compare a treatment group receiving a one-shot manipulation of the head of fibula against a comparison/control group (with study procedures also noting randomized allocation approaches).

brief_summary: This phase II trial studies how well a vaccine called Nous-209 works in reducing the size of abnormal area of tissue growth or polyps (colorectal lesions) in patients with Lynch syndrome. When patients have Lynch syndrome, errors in the genetic information inside cells are not properly corrected. When that happens, the cells produce new proteins called neoantigens. Nous-209 is a vaccine with man-made copies of neoantigens combined with viral vectors. Neoantigens are new proteins that form inside tumor cells when certain mutations occur inside them. The body's immune system recognizes these proteins as foreign and generates a response against the tumor cell that produced the neoantigen. Giving the Nous-209 vaccine may be able to reduce the size of existing colorectal lesions (polyps) that were 5 to 15 mm in diameter at the time of patients' first colonoscopy or flexible sigmoidoscopy.
interventions: Adenoviral Tumor-specific Neoantigen Priming Vaccine GAd-209-FSP

Samples from the nares, skin, and stool will be collected at each of the 10 study visits to detect S. aureus and B. subtilis. We will also conduct interviews to assess acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility of the probiotic and study regimen.

brief_summary:
Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is a subtype of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL), characterized by a heterogeneous clinical course and, in a substantial proportion of patients, an aggressive disease behavior requiring timely and effective treatment at diagnosis.

In recent years, the therapeutic landscape of MCL has undergone a major transformation with the introduction of Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis). Ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, and the non-covalent BTKi pirtobrutinib have demonstrated substantial clinical activity in relapsed/refractry (R/R) MCL. Their role has progressively expanded beyond the relapsed/refractory setting, with BTK inhibitor-based regimens increasingly being incorporated into frontline treatment strategies, supported by emerging clinical trial evidence and reflected in evolving treatment guidelines and clinical practice.

Despite this rapidly evolving treatment landscape, real-world evidence on the use of BTKi-based regimens in the frontline setting remains limited. In particular, data on treatment selection, efficacy, safety, treatment duration, and management of toxicities in routine clinical practice are still scarce.

We therefore propose an observational cohort study to evaluate the clinical impact of previously untreated patients with MCL receiving frontline BTKi-based regimens in routine clinical practice in Italy. The study will assess treatment patterns, effectiveness, safety, and treatment persistence, providing real-world insights into the use of these strategies beyond clinical trials.
title: Observational Study to Evaluate the Clinical Impact of BTK Inhibitor-Based Regimens in Treatment-Naïve Patients With Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL) in Italian Clinical Practice.

brief_summary:

Approximately 90 students will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group using block randomization.The intervention group will receive simulation-based education involving high-risk childbirth scenarios, while the control group will receive conventional education covering the same topics. The educational program will last six weeks, with one session per week. The training will focus on the management of obstetric emergencies, including postpartum hemorrhage, shoulder dystocia, preeclampsia, and placenta previa.

Data will be collected using a participant information form, the Simulation-Based Learning Evaluation Scale, and the Nursing Anxiety and Self-Confidence with Clinical Decision-Making Scale. Both groups will be assessed before and after the educational intervention.The study aims to determine whether artificial intelligence-assisted simulation-based education improves learning experiences and clinical decision-making self-confidence while reducing anxiety compared with conventional education. Following the post-intervention assessments, participants will be offered the alternative educational approach to ensure equal learning opportunities.
title: AI-Assisted High-Risk Childbirth Simulation in Midwifery Education

Adults with chronic respiratory disease who need oxygen during exertion perform two six-minute walk tests on the same day, 30 minutes apart: one with oxygen adjusted automatically by EMILY.AI and one with a fixed oxygen flow delivered through the same device. The order is randomized and participants do not know which test uses automatic titration.

brief_summary:
An adequate width of keratinized gingiva is important for maintaining periodontal and peri-implant tissue health. Free gingival grafting (FGG) is a commonly performed surgical procedure for increasing insufficient keratinized gingival width. This study aims to evaluate the effect of applying a chitosan sponge to the palatal donor site on wound healing after FGG using exfoliative cytology and to compare the findings with those obtained from a control group in which no chitosan sponge is applied.

At least 40 patients scheduled to undergo FGG because of insufficient keratinized gingival width will be included. The patients will be allocated to two groups: a test group and a control group. In the test group, a chitosan sponge will be applied to the palatal donor site, whereas no wound dressing will be applied to the palatal donor site in the control group. The primary outcome will be the keratinization index determined from cytological samples collected from the palatal donor site at one month after surgery. The keratinization index values at one month will be compared between the test and control groups.

All participants will receive detailed information about the study and the procedures, and written informed consent will be obtained. Clinical measurements will be recorded before surgery, after which the FGG procedure will be performed. Depending on group allocation, the palatal donor site will either be treated with a chitosan sponge or left without a wound dressing. Sutures will be removed on postoperative day 10.

For exfoliative cytological assessment, baseline samples will be collected from both the planned palatal donor site and the contralateral symmetrical healthy palatal site, which will not undergo surgery, in all patients. Samples collected from the symmetrical palatal site will serve as a reference for the baseline characteristics of healthy palatal mucosa. Follow-up samples will be collected exclusively from the palatal donor site on postoperative day 3,10 and at 1, 3, and 6 months. The keratinization index and other cellular features associated with wound healing will be assessed in the cytological samples. Findings obtained during the follow-up periods will be compared between the test group treated with a chitosan sponge and the control group in which no wound dressing is applied. In addition, the presence or absence of sensory loss at the palatal donor site will be evaluated using a periodontal probe.
title: Cytological Assessment of Donor-Site Healing After Free Gingival Grafting

brief_summary:
This study tests whether adding a rumination-focused training module to an 8-week online mindfulness program helps reduce emotional distress and repetitive negative thinking (rumination) more than the mindfulness program on its own.

When people feel distressed, many get caught in cycles of repeatedly going over worries or upsetting experiences-a habit called rumination. This study aims to find out whether teaching specific skills to notice and respond helpfully to rumination, in addition to a standard mindfulness program, leads to better outcomes.

About 150 Chinese adults aged 18 to 65 who report elevated emotional distress and elevated rumination will take part. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) a standard online mindfulness program (Mindfulness Intervention for Emotional Distress, MIED); (2) the same mindfulness program with an added rumination-targeted module; or (3) a wait-list control group that is offered the standard mindfulness program free of charge after the study period.

The programs run for 8 weeks. All participants complete the same set of questionnaires at four time points: before starting, around weeks 3 and 5, and within 7 days after the program ends. The main outcome is emotional distress, measured with the K10 scale. Rumination, depression, anxiety, and mindfulness are also measured.

The results will help clarify whether adding rumination-focused training is feasible and beneficial, and whether earlier reductions in rumination help explain later improvements in emotional distress. The study does not promise a cure or guaranteed individual improvement.

brief_summary:
For Couples undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF), one of the most important decisions is choosing which embryo has the best chance of leading to a healthy pregnancy. Today, this often relies on a biopsy, where a few cells are removed from the embryo for genetic testing (PGT-A). This technique has shown high accuracy; however, this test is invasive, adds cost, and involves handling the embryo directly.

The Prediction of Embryo Aneuploidy using Non-invasive Morphokinetics and Culture Media Readouts (PEARL) Trial is testing a non-invasive alternative that combines two approaches. The first; time-lapse imaging using a camera-equipped incubator to continuously record how an embryo divides and grows, without ever removing it from its stable environment. The second; spent culture media testing by analyzing the fluid that the embryo grows in for biological signals (DNA fragments, microRNA, proteins, and metabolic byproducts) which the embryo releases as it develops.

By studying these two sources of information together, alongside each embryo's actual genetic result from standard PGT-A testing, we aim to find out whether imaging and fluid analysis, combined, can reliably predict whether an embryo is chromosomally normal (euploid) or abnormal (aneuploid) without needing a biopsy.

Taking part does not change a couple's standard IVF treatment. Embryos are cultured and tested exactly as they normally would be; the only difference is that imaging data and a small sample of fluid that would otherwise be thrown away are collected for research analysis. All embryo selection and transfer decisions continue to be based on the clinic's usual standard of care.

If successful, this approach could make embryo assessment safer, faster, and more affordable reducing the need for invasive testing in IVF, in Abu Dhabi and internationally.

brief_summary: In the United States, children who are not breastfed are advised to drink whole cow's milk from age 1 and switch to low-fat (1%) or non-fat milk at age 2. There is little trial evidence behind this switch, and some observational studies link lower-fat milk to higher body weight in children. This pilot study tested whether a larger, longer randomized trial of milk fat type in young children would be feasible and acceptable to families. Parents of young children in the San Francisco Bay Area were randomly assigned to give their child either whole milk or non-fat (or low-fat 1%) milk, delivered free to their home for 3 months. At the start and after 3 months, the study team measured the child's growth, development, diet, blood lipids, vitamin D level, and gut bacteria. brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized online study is to learn how different features of premium cigar advertisements affect adults' perceptions of premium cigars and their intentions to purchase or use them. The main questions are whether advertisements that include hertiage claims, alcohol imagery, or manufcaturing claims affect perceptions of product appeal, taste, freshness, smoothness, quality, and health risks, and whether these features affect intentions to purchase and use the product.

Approximately 2,000 adults living in the United States who have used premium cigars in the past year will complete an online survey about demographics and tobacco use. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of four conditions. They will then view three premium cigar advertisements containing a specific feature (i.e., alcohol, brand heritage, manufacturing). A control group will view ads without these features. Participants will then answer questions about the advertisements, premium cigars, and their intentions to purchase or use them.
lead_sponsor: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
title: Premium Cigar Advertising

brief_summary:
Neuroendocrine tumors are rare tumors with prolonged survival. The management of patients at advanced stage is centered on both locoregional control and systemic therapy. Systemic approaches include somatostatin analogs (SSA) that improve symptom control and slow tumor progression, peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), targeted agents (everolimus, sunitinib and cabozantinib) and chemotherapy. All these therapies have demonstrated clinical benefit across multiple randomized and non-randomized studies, yet no high-level evidence defines the optimal sequence in which they should be administered in real-world metastatic settings.

The recent approval of cabozantinib, a multikinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR, MET, and AXL, represents a major advancement in the systemic management of NETs.

The retrospective study "CARE-NET", is a multicenter study which has the aims to describe the real-world use of cabozantinib (between January 2020 and August 2026) in France.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate, in real-world clinical practice, the Disease Control Rate (DCR) achieved with cabozantinib among patients with advanced or metastatic well-differentiated NETs treated between January 2020 and August 2026.
title: Real-World Effectiveness of Cabozantinib in Advanced Neuroendocrine Tumors: A Retrospective Multicenter Study Using the GTE-RENATEN National Database

brief_summary: This study examined the relationship between affective temperament (relatively stable emotional traits) and lower back movement in adults with mechanically provoked low back pain. It also described changes in pain and lower back movement during a two-week Cyriax physiotherapy program. The study was conducted at one rehabilitation clinic in Bydgoszcz, Poland, during 2016-2018 and included 100 adults (73 women and 27 men). All participants received ten individual, in-person physiotherapy sessions of 30 minutes each over two consecutive weeks. There was one treatment group, with no random assignment, comparison group, or blinded outcome assessment. Temperament was assessed before treatment; pain and lower back movement were assessed before and immediately after the program. This is a retrospective registration of a completed study. The study was not prospectively registered. Its exploratory analyses cannot establish that physiotherapy caused any observed changes.
primary_outcomes: Lumbar Left Rotation Range of Motion

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the acute effects of consuming traditional processed meat products with reduced sodium content on blood pressure and urinary sodium excretion in healthy adults.

The study will compare the effects of traditional products with reformulated versions containing 25% and 50% less sodium. The products under evaluation include traditional Portuguese processed meat products such as "alheira", "chouriça" and "butelo".

Participants will consume the different product formulations according to a controlled study protocol.

Blood pressure will be assessed, and urine samples will be collected over a 24-hour period to evaluate sodium excretion.

This study is part of a research project focused on developing healthier traditional meat products while preserving their characteristic sensory properties. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the effects of sodium reduction in processed meat products on cardiovascular health.
conditions: Dietary Sodium Intake and Blood Pressure
primary_outcomes: Changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure following consumption of processed meat products with different sodium contents
title: Effect of Consuming Processed Meat Products With Reduced Sodium on Cardiometabolic Risk Biomarkers

brief_summary: The goal of this observational study is to investigate cardiovascular risks and long-term outcomes in adults with cancer in China. Researchers will collect clinical information from medical records and follow participants over time to assess cardiovascular health and outcomes.Participants in the prospective cohort will undergo cardiovascular assessments and follow-up as part of their clinical care. brief_summary: This randomized, controlled, crossover dietary intervention will test whether a three-week diverse diet, compared with a control diet with lower food diversity, changes postprandial insulin responses, other metabolic parameters, and the gut microbiome in 34 healthy adults with overweight. Participants will complete both diets in a randomized order, separated by a four-week washout period. The intervention periods will be conducted under free-living conditions, with study foods provided by the research center. Before and after each intervention period, postprandial metabolism will be assessed using standardized meal tests conducted under controlled whole-room calorimetry conditions. The primary outcome is the log-transformed total postprandial insulin area under the concentration-time curve from 0 to 240 minutes.
title: Impact of Dietary Diversity on Postprandial Insulin Secretion and Metabolism

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the size of the port (trocar) used to remove the appendix during laparoscopic appendectomy affects whether the appendix is removed intact. The study includes adults (18 years and older) who undergo laparoscopic surgery for acute appendicitis.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does removing the appendix through a 12 mm trocar, compared with a 10 mm trocar, reduce damage (tearing or fragmentation) to the removed appendix?

Keeping the appendix intact is important because cancer is sometimes found unexpectedly in removed appendices, and a damaged specimen can make the pathology assessment and further treatment decisions difficult.

Researchers will also compare the two groups for operation time, length of hospital stay, pain after surgery, wound and abdominal infections, bleeding, and hernia at the port site.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of two groups: the appendix will be removed through either a 10 mm or a 12 mm trocar during standard laparoscopic appendectomy
* Rate their pain after surgery using a visual analog scale
* Be followed for complications after surgery
interventions: Specimen extraction through a 10 mm trocar
Specimen extraction through a 12 mm trocar
title: Specimen Integrity in Laparoscopic Appendectomy

brief_summary: This study is a retrospective non-interventional cohort study, utilizing real-world administrative claim data and electronic health record data associated with the medical insurance database in Nanjing, China (2019-2026). The study aims to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of PCSK9 monoclonal antibody（evolocumab, alirocumab, tafolecimab, ongericimab, recaticimab and ebronucimab） versus cholesterol absorption inhibitors (ezetimibe and hyzetimibe) as add-on lipid-lowering therapy in adults undergoing secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (ASCVD). Outcomes include composite CVD, three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), fatal CVD, all-cause mortality, discontinuation, and persistence. Direct medical costs will be estimated from third-party payer and healthcare system perspectives. Cost-effectiveness will be expressed in terms of the incremental cost per prevented MACE), the number needed to treat (NNT), and the incremental cost per prevented all-cause death. Sensitivity analyses will assess robustness. Findings are intended to inform clinical selection, reimbursement, and dynamic adjustment of the medical insurance directory for ASCVD secondary prevention.
title: Real-World Study Comparing PCSK9 Monoclonal Antibody With Cholesterol Absorption Inhibitors in Patients With ASCVD for Secondary Prevention

brief_summary:
Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC) accounts for approximately 5% of RCC cases and has distinct morphological and molecular features. However, advanced chRCC follows an aggressive clinical course and responds poorly to standard regimens developed for clear cell RCC.

Lenvatinib plus everolimus (LEN+EVE) has demonstrated clinical activity in clear cell RCC (Study 205), with responses also reported in non-clear cell subtypes, including chRCC. Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab (LEN+PEMBRO) demonstrated a high objective response rate (ORR) in KEYNOTE-B61, including in the chRCC subgroup.

These findings support conducting a prospective phase 2 study specifically dedicated to this rare subtype to provide direct evidence of the efficacy and safety of these two active combinations.
title: Combinations With Lenvatinib in Patients With Metastatic Chromophobe Renal Cell Carcinoma: a Phase 2 Study.

brief_summary:
This study is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial designed to evaluate the effects of a combination of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. longum strains on stress-related health outcomes in adults. The study plans to enroll 126 adults experiencing stress-related problems, who will be randomly assigned in equal proportions to either the probiotic group or the placebo group and will receive the assigned intervention for 8 weeks. Participants will complete the scheduled study visits and assessments.

The study will systematically evaluate the principal health concerns of young adults experiencing high levels of stress through multiple approaches, including subjective questionnaire assessments, biological sample testing, and gut microbiome analysis. The main assessments will include a comparison of changes in stress status before and after the intervention between the probiotic and placebo groups using validated psychological assessment instruments. The effects of the intervention on sleep quality, quality of life, and related emotional states will also be evaluated. Sleep quality and quality of life will be assessed using validated assessment instruments.

To further investigate the potential biological mechanisms, stool samples will be collected from participants for gut microbiome metagenomic analysis to characterize changes in microbial composition and functional features. Laboratory-based assays will also be used to measure stress-, immune-, and inflammation-related biomarkers. This study is expected to provide preliminary evidence supporting the clinical application of microbiota-targeted interventions based on modulation of the gut-brain axis in populations experiencing high levels of stress.
primary_outcomes: Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-42 (DASS-42) Stress Subscale Score
title: Effects of a Combination of Bifidobacterium Longum Subsp. Longum Strains on Stress and Related Health Outcomes in Young Adult

brief_summary:
Multiple sclerosis is a chronic neurological disease that can cause muscle weakness, impaired walking, and difficulty controlling ankle movement. Foot drop is a common gait impairment in people with multiple sclerosis and occurs when weakness of the ankle dorsiflexor muscles limits the ability to lift the foot during walking.

This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to compare the effects of eccentric and concentric ankle dorsiflexor resistance training on ankle muscle strength and dynamic plantar pressure parameters during walking in adults with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and foot drop.

A total of 54 participants are planned for enrollment. Eligible participants will be randomly allocated to two parallel groups, with 27 participants assigned to each group. The first group will perform eccentric ankle dorsiflexor training, while the second group will perform concentric ankle dorsiflexor training. Both groups will also receive the same standardized conventional physical therapy program.

The intervention will consist of three treatment sessions per week for six weeks, with each session lasting approximately 45 minutes. Ankle dorsiflexor resistance training will be performed using graded elastic resistance bands.

The primary outcome measures will be concentric and eccentric ankle dorsiflexor peak torque, assessed using a HUMAC NORM isokinetic dynamometer. Secondary outcome measures will include total plantar force, maximum plantar pressure, plantar contact surface area, and plantar contact time during walking, assessed using the DIERS pedoscan plantar pressure measurement system.

Measurements will be obtained before and after the six-week intervention period. The study will determine whether eccentric and concentric ankle dorsiflexor training produce different effects on muscle strength and dynamic plantar loading in individuals with multiple sclerosis and foot drop.
interventions: standardized Conventional Physical Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis
title: Eccentric vs. Concentric Ankle Training in Multiple Sclerosis

brief_summary:
Chronic nonspecific low back pain is a common musculoskeletal condition associated with pain, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life. Therapeutic exercise is widely recommended for its management, while structured breathing techniques may provide additional benefits through their potential influence on respiratory function, trunk muscle coordination, and postural control.

The purpose of this randomized controlled trial was to investigate whether incorporating structured breathing into a supervised therapeutic exercise program provides additional benefits compared with performing the same exercises with spontaneous breathing.

Thirty adults with chronic nonspecific low back pain were randomly allocated to two groups: structured breathing (SB) or spontaneous breathing (SpB). Both groups participated in an eight-week supervised exercise program consisting of three sessions per week, lasting approximately 45 minutes each. The program combined trunk muscle activation, stabilization, mobility, and flexibility exercises. Participants in the SB group received additional instructions to coordinate breathing with movement, whereas participants in the SpB group performed the same exercises without prescribed breathing patterns.

Assessments were conducted before and after the intervention and included pain intensity, functional disability, fear-avoidance, spinal mobility, abdominal drawing-in performance, pulmonary function, cardiorespiratory fitness, and heart rate recovery.

The study was designed to evaluate the additional effects of structured breathing when integrated into an otherwise comparable therapeutic exercise program for individuals with chronic nonspecific low back pain.
title: Structured Versus Spontaneous Breathing During an Integrated Multimodal Exercise Program for Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs) are potentially life-threatening vascular lesions that may rupture and cause aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a condition associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. The prevalence of UIAs in the general population is approximately 3.2%. Current guidelines recommend screening primarily for individuals with a strong family history of UIA/SAH or autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). However, these groups account for only a minority of patients with UIAs.

Smoking is a major modifiable risk factor for UIA formation and rupture. Preliminary studies suggest that UIA prevalence may be substantially higher among smokers than in the general population, but prospective data are limited, particularly in men.

This prospective screening study aims to determine the prevalence of UIAs in active and recent smokers aged 30-60 years with a smoking history of at least 10 pack-years. We hypothesize that UIA prevalence in this population is significantly higher than in the general population and may approach that of established high-risk groups.

Participants will undergo non-contrast 3T magnetic resonance angiography (time-of-flight sequence). Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, smoking habits, nicotine dependence, and quality of life will be assessed using REDCap questionnaires. Imaging findings will be communicated to participants, and those with detected aneurysms or relevant incidental findings will be referred for standard clinical evaluation. At 30 (±14) days after MRI, smoking habits, nicotine dependence, quality of life, and consequences of screening will be reassessed. The study will also evaluate the clinical implications and costs of screening.
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern
primary_outcomes: percentage of Unruptured intracranial aneurysms detected by screening
title: Swiss Pilot Screening Study for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms to Prevent Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Smokers

brief_summary:
Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity, mainly infectious complications and postoperative pancreatic fistula. Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis is routine, but the optimal strategy for postoperative antibiotic administration is unclear, and practice varies between surgeons.

The objective of this study is to determine whether the duration of postoperative piperacillin-tazobactam (24 hours versus 5 days) affects postoperative infectious outcomes in patients undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy.

This is a single-center, prospective, randomized clinical trial in adults undergoing open or minimally invasive (robotic) pancreaticoduodenectomy. All consented patients receive perioperative piperacillin-tazobactam according to institutional practice. After the operation is completed, patients who underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy and remain eligible are randomized by a computerized system, stratified by presence of a preoperative biliary stent and by surgical approach, to postoperative antibiotic treatment for 24 hours or 5 days.

The primary endpoint is the rate of postoperative infectious complications, comprising superficial wound infection, deep (fascial) surgical site infection, and intra-abdominal infection, defined according to CDC criteria, \[within 30 days after surgery\]. Participation does not change surgical technique, length of hospitalization, or routine follow-up.

As an exploratory component, intraoperative bile cultures are collected to describe biliary microbial profiles and antibiotic resistance patterns.

The study aims to provide high-quality evidence to guide postoperative antibiotic management and support more rational use of broad-spectrum antibiotics in pancreatic surgery.
primary_outcomes: Rate of surgical site infection (SSI) after pancreaticoduodenectomy
title: Prospective Randomized Trial Protocol for Duration of Post-Operative Tazocin Treatment After Whipple Operation

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to assess the immediate effects of cervical joint mobilization on patients experiencing neck-shoulder pain.

The main research questions are: (1) Does the joint mobilization intervention acutely change blood flow in the neck/shoulder area? (2) Does the joint mobilization intervention acutely increase pressure pain thresholds (PPTs)? (3) Does the joint mobilization intervention acutely increase cervical range of motion (ROM)? (4) Does the joint mobilization intervention acutely decrease the number of tender and hypertonic points?

This study utilizes a single-session, pre- and post-intervention design with no comparison group. Participants will attend one on-site visit (1.25 hours) for screening and intervention. First, each eligible participant will complete an intake form for demographics and three questionnaires: the Brief Pain Index (BPI), Neck Disability Index (NDI), and Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI).

Following the questionnaires, participants will undergo baseline assessments for their tender and hypertonic points, cervical ROMs, PPTs, and blood flow parameter. After the baseline assessments, each participant will receive a lateral glide oscillatory joint mobilization technique to the C4-C5 level for five minutes. Immediately following the intervention, all four outcome measures, including tender points, cervical ROM, PPTs and blood flow parameters will be re-assessed.
title: Effects of Cervical Joint Mobilization on Blood Flow, Hypersensitivity to Pressure and Neck Motions

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether DLBS1442 can alleviate primary dysmenorrhea in young adults aged 18 to 21 years. The main question it aims to answer is:

1\. Does DLBS1442, at doses of 100 mg and 200 mg, reduce dysmenorrhea pain compared with placebo, as measured by the change from baseline in Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score at predefined time points after the first dose?

Researchers will compare DLBS1442 100 mg, DLBS1442 200 mg, with placebo to determine whether DLBS1442 is more effective in reducing dysmenorrhea pain.

Participants will:

1. Take DLBS1442 or placebo three times daily for up to 5 consecutive days during one menstrual cycle. Treatment may be discontinued earlier if pain completely resolves (VAS = 0).
2. Return to the study site on Day 6 after Visit 1 for assessment of study drug compliance, diary review, return of unused study medication and packaging, and study-related evaluations.
3. Record the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score before each study drug administration.
4. Complete the quality-of-life questionnaire on Days 1, 2, 3, and 6.
5. Record any adverse events and concomitant medications used throughout the study.
6. Record the use of rescue medication (paracetamol), including the VAS pain score immediately before each rescue medication dose.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) Pain Score Within 6 Hours After the First Dose
title: The Efficacy and Safety of DLBS1442 in Patients With Primary Dysmenorrhea

brief_summary:
Some people with heart failure develop fluid buildup in the lungs and need a breathing machine while they are treated in an intensive care unit. The amount of air delivered with each breath may affect how quickly they recover.

The LOGICAL study will compare two ways of setting the breathing machine: delivering a lower or an intermediate amount of air with each breath. About 300 adults in intensive care units across Spain will be randomly assigned to one of these strategies.

The study aims to find out whether the lower amount of air increases the number of days patients are alive and breathing without the machine during the first 28 days after assignment. The researchers will also assess other outcomes, including survival and length of stay in the intensive care unit and hospital.

brief_summary:
This study aimed to investigate the effects of short-term Rhodiola rosea supplementation on anaerobic exercise performance and blood lactate responses during post-exercise recovery in trained male athletes.

The study used a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design involving 23 trained men. Each participant completed two experimental conditions: Rhodiola rosea supplementation and placebo, administered in a randomized order with a 5-day washout period between conditions.

During the Rhodiola rosea condition, participants received 1,500 mg per day for three consecutive days, followed by an additional 500 mg dose 30 minutes before exercise testing. The placebo condition followed an identical administration schedule without the active supplement.

Following each supplementation condition, participants performed a 30-second Wingate Anaerobic Test to assess anaerobic performance. Blood lactate concentrations were measured before exercise and at 3, 10, and 20 minutes after exercise.

The study was designed to determine whether short-term Rhodiola rosea supplementation influences maximal anaerobic performance and blood lactate concentrations during recovery from high-intensity exercise.
primary_outcomes: Peak Power During the 30-Second Wingate Anaerobic Test
title: Effects of Rhodiola Rosea Supplementation on Anaerobic Performance and Blood Lactate in Trained Men

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether offering same-day co-administration of the varicella (chickenpox) vaccine and the inactivated hepatitis A vaccine at routine vaccination clinics helps children in China complete both vaccines on time, and how parents feel about this service.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do parents accept same-day administration of the two vaccines when clinics offer this option?
* Are children more likely to complete both vaccines within 90 days when the same-day option is available?

Participants will receive routine vaccination care as usual. After clinic staff explain the options - both vaccines on the same day at different injection sites, on different days, or waiting - parents freely choose, and the study records the choice. Families who take part receive short follow-up contacts about 1 week, 1 month, and 6 weeks after each vaccination to ask about fever, rash, or other health problems, complete a short satisfaction survey at 1 month, and are followed for 90 days through immunization records. Results will also be compared with de-identified immunization records of similar children from the same clinics before the service was introduced.
primary_outcomes: Completion rate of both vaccines within 90 days
title: Timeliness, Parental Acceptability, and Safety of Same-Day Administration of Varicella and Hepatitis A Vaccines Among Children: An Observational Study

brief_summary:
This study evaluates the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of contextually adapted AVATAR therapy for people experiencing distressing voices associated with psychosis in Ethiopia and India. AVATAR therapy is a psychological intervention in which participants create a digital avatar representing a distressing voice and engage in therapist-supported dialogues with the avatar.

Thirty participants (15 in Ethiopia and 15 in India) will receive culturally adapted AVATAR therapy. Participants will complete assessments at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks. The study will assess feasibility of recruitment and retention, acceptability of the intervention, safety, and preliminary changes in voice-related distress, beliefs about voices, emotional wellbeing, and functioning. Qualitative interviews will explore participants' and therapists' experiences of the intervention and its cultural relevance.
primary_outcomes: Acceptability of AVATAR Therapy: Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8)
Acceptability: Acceptability of Intervention measure (AIM) service user rating
Safety of AVATAR therapy assessed through monitoring of adverse events
Acceptability: Acceptability of Intervention measure (AIM) therapist rating
