brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective observational study is to investigate if a point-of-care testing device using microfluidics can evaluate the biophysical characteristics of white blood cells for the rapid diagnosis and prognosis of acute infection or sepsis.

Our main aim is to develop a rapid biophysical sparing assay protocol for the diagnosis and/or prognosis of acute infection and sepsis in the ED among patients with non-specific symptoms, by differentiating infection vs. non-infection in febrile cases, viral vs. bacterial cause of infection (if infection present) and low vs. high risk of sepsis with organ dysfunction.
interventions: Microfluidic device for assessment of biophysical properties of white blood cells
primary_outcomes: Infective vs. no infection in febrile cases
Viral vs. bacterial cause of infection (if infection present)
Low vs. high risk of sepsis with organ dysfunction
title: Immune Response Profiling in Sepsis

brief_summary:
This study investigated whether multitarget high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS), combined with cognitive learning strategies, could improve temporal order memory during spatial navigation in patients with schizophrenia.

Schizophrenia is frequently associated with cognitive impairments, including difficulties remembering the order of events and navigating unfamiliar environments. This study examined whether noninvasive electrical brain stimulation could enhance the benefits of repeated memory testing compared with repeated studying.

In this randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled study, 59 hospitalized patients with schizophrenia were assigned to receive either active or sham HD-tDCS while completing a spatial navigation learning task. Both groups performed forward-testing and restudy conditions. Active stimulation was delivered for 20 minutes, and spatial navigation learning lasted approximately 45 minutes.

Spatial navigation memory was evaluated using landmark-order recall accuracy. Resting-state functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was performed before and after the intervention to examine changes in functional connectivity between prefrontal and parietal brain regions.

The study aimed to determine whether multitarget HD-tDCS could improve spatial navigation memory, enhance the benefits of forward testing, and influence functional connectivity in brain networks involved in cognitive control and spatial attention.
lead_sponsor: School of Psychology, Northwest Normal University
title: Multitarget HD-tDCS and Spatial Navigation Memory in Schizophrenia

brief_summary: The main purpose of this study is to demonstrate the superiority of pacibekitug compared to placebo in reducing the risk of 3-point coronary major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-Coronary- MACE), defined as a composite of coronary heart disease (CHD) death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and urgent coronary revascularization, in participants after an MI, at high cardiovascular (CV) risk and receiving standard of care (SoC) secondary CV prevention therapies.
primary_outcomes: Time to the first occurrence of 3P-Coronary-MACE
title: A Study to Assess the Effect of Pacibekitug on Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients After a Myocardial Infarction

brief_summary:
Sarcomas with the EWSR1/FUS :: POU2AF3 (COLCA2) fusion transcript represent a new molecularly defined entity, first described in 2023 (1). There are 24 cases reported in the literature, including 3 descriptive series totaling 19 cases (1-3). Clinically, this is an aggressive entity affecting patients of varying ages (16-74 years), most commonly located in the sinonasal tract, and capable of involving both bone and soft tissue. A few extrasinonasal cases have also been reported. Histologically, two morphological groups have been described (3): the first group (the rarest) is characterized by a low-grade morphology with non-atypical spindle cells; the second group is morphologically high-grade, featuring spindle, round, or epithelioid cells and possible divergent differentiation (epithelial, neuroendocrine, striated muscle, or bone).

The immunophenotype of these lesions is nonspecific, with variable positivity for various markers such as S100, CD99, AE1/3, CD56, chromogranin, synaptophysin, SATB2, CD117, GFAP, and EMA.

Given the clinical, morphological, and immunohistochemical features of this entity, numerous differential diagnoses can be considered: synovial sarcoma, malignant tumor of the peripheral nerve sheaths, Ewing sarcoma, myoepithelial tumor, biphenotypic sinonasal sarcoma, etc.
primary_outcomes: Clustering Common to methylation analysis and RNA-seq.
title: Sarcoma With EWSR1/FUS : POU2AF3 (COLCA2) Fusion : Molecular and Clinicopathologic Characterization of a Case Series.

brief_summary: How can investigators improve recurrence rates of chronic subdural hematomas to reduce need for surgical intervention? Study investigators hypothesize that Dextrose 5% in 0.225% Sodium Chloride (D5 ¼NS) will increase the intracellular brain volume and water content post-operatively, reducing the residual subdural space that is created by evacuation of the chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH), and that this, in turn, will reduce the hematoma volume that will then potentially lead to improved functional outcomes, reduced hospitalization time as well as the reduced rate of symptomatic recurrence requiring redo surgery.
primary_outcomes: Comparative residual CSDH volume (in mm3) measured and calculated using head CT
title: Chronic Subdural Hematoma Recurrence

brief_summary: This study will include infants seen at three hospitals who have a segmental infantile hemangioma, a blood vessel growth affecting a broad area of skin. Eligible areas include the scalp, face, neck, upper chest or back, and shoulder or upper arm. The study will measure how often PHACE syndrome is found in infants with enough clinical information to determine the diagnosis. PHACE syndrome can involve differences in the development of the brain, arteries, heart, eyes, or the midline of the chest and abdomen. The study team will describe these findings and the hemangiomas. The treating clinicians will manage evaluation and care.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Evaluable Infants With PHACE Syndrome
title: Incidence and Clinical Features of PHACE Syndrome

brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effect of the 4-7-8 structured breathing exercise on perceived stress, psychological resilience, and sleep quality among first-year university students.

The transition to university life can be a significant source of stress, affecting students' well-being and sleep. In this study, min. 64 first-year nursing students will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will receive training and practice the 4-7-8 breathing exercise for four weeks, every night before sleep. The control group will continue their usual daily routines without any new relaxation interventions. Researchers will measure participants' perceived stress, psychological resilience, and sleep quality at baseline and after the 4-week intervention period to compare the outcomes between the two groups.
title: The Effect of the 4-7-8 Breathing Exercise on Stress, Resilience, and Sleep Quality in First-Year University Students

brief_summary:
This clinical study aims to develop and apply early-warning and precision-intervention technologies for older adults with declining intrinsic capacity. It intends to identify key digital biomarkers, build dynamic prediction models, and verify the effectiveness of a human-computer interactive adaptive closed-loop intervention system, so as to shift geriatric health management from reactive medical care to proactive health management. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can multi-modal digital data enable early warning of intrinsic capacity decline among community-dwelling older adults?

Does the AI-driven personalized stepped intervention reduce the incidence of intrinsic capacity decline and adverse health events in older adults?Researchers will compare an integrated whole-course intrinsic-capacity management platform intervention versus routine community-based geriatric health services through a cluster-randomized controlled trial.Participants will:

Complete baseline multi-modal assessments including standard scales and wearable-device-based physiological monitoring Receive follow-up assessments every 3-6 months for 12-24 months in the cohort phase Be assigned to either the intervention group or the control group for a 6-month intervention period Undergo multi-dimensional evaluations at baseline, month 3, month 6 and month 12 Comply with health-management requirements or routine community health services according to group assignment
interventions: IC Management Platform with AI Health Coach
lead_sponsor: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
title: Early- Warning and Precision-Intervention Technologies for Decline in Intrinsic Capacity

brief_summary: This prospective observational cohort study will evaluate the diagnostic performance and workflow feasibility of a prespecified locked artificial intelligence model that analyzes smartphone-based natural-light gross images of fresh surgical tissue together with participant age. Approximately 400 consecutive adults undergoing initial surgery for suspected intracranial adult-type diffuse glioma will be enrolled at Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between July and September 2026. Images will be acquired before frozen-section processing according to a standardized operating procedure. Model outputs will be generated in silent mode and will not be shown to the surgical or pathology teams and will not alter diagnosis or treatment. The locked model score will be compared with the final IDH mutation reference standard derived from permanent histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and indicated molecular testing. The primary objective is to estimate patient-level discrimination for IDH-mutant versus IDH-wildtype tumors. Secondary objectives include fixed-threshold performance, precision-recall performance, calibration, end-to-end technical success, and prespecified model abstention, if an abstention rule is locked before enrollment.
interventions: Smartphone Nature-image AI prediction of IDH status (SNAP-IDH)
primary_outcomes: Patient-Level Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve of the Locked SNAP-IDH Score for IDH Mutation Status
title: Prospective Study of Intraoperative Brain Tumor Photographs for Pathological and Molecular Classification

brief_summary:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries, particularly non-contact injuries, are among the most common injuries in team sports and frequently occur during cutting maneuvers. They are associated with a substantial risk of secondary injuries, especially in pediatric and adolescent athletes. Persistent biomechanical alterations, neurocognitive deficits, and suboptimal movement strategies may contribute to the risk of re-injury even after ACL reconstruction and return to sport.

The diagnosis of ACL injury and the indication for surgical treatment are primarily based on clinical assessment, including tests such as the anterior drawer, Lachman, and pivot shift tests, which evaluate anteroposterior laxity and rotational instability. Instrumented assessments, including the KT-1000 and KiRA accelerometer, can provide objective measurements of knee laxity and complement the clinical evaluation.

Several ACL reconstruction techniques and graft types are currently available, with the main goal of restoring anteroposterior and rotational knee stability, recovering function, and reducing the risk of subsequent injury. Despite favorable clinical outcomes and high rates of return to sport, athletes may continue to show deficits in neuromuscular control, functional performance, and high-intensity movement patterns after rehabilitation and return to sport.

Conventional return-to-sport assessments may therefore fail to detect residual deficits, particularly during dynamic and sport-specific movements. This highlights the need for objective and multidimensional assessment methods capable of quantitatively evaluating movement quality under ecologically valid conditions.

Although optoelectronic motion capture systems represent the gold standard for movement analysis, their use is mainly restricted to controlled laboratory settings, which may not fully reproduce the demands and natural movement patterns of sports activities. In contrast, wearable inertial sensors and markerless motion analysis based on pose-estimation algorithms allow objective, non-invasive, and ecologically valid assessment of complex movements in both clinical and sporting environments.

Given the high risk of re-injury and the evidence of persistent biomechanical alterations following ACL reconstruction, investigating movement patterns during sport-specific tasks is therefore of particular interest. Integrating wearable sensors and markerless motion analysis and comparing ACL-reconstructed athletes with healthy individuals may help identify residual biomechanical and neuromuscular alterations that are not detectable through conventional clinical assessment alone.
title: Study of the Integrated Biomechanics of the Lower Limbs and Trunk in Athletes of Different Age Groups During the Performance of Motor Tasks

brief_summary: This is a non-interventional study being conducted to validate the performance of a machine learning algorithm for prediction of eGFR from digital retinal images in a target population for future intended use as a populated-based screening tool. Secondary objectives will include prediction of blood pressure (\> or ≤ 140/90 mmHg) and presence or absence of T2DM as determined by glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c \>6.5%) or on the basis of clinical history. Once validated, the methodology will be deployed for health screening to improve access to healthcare.
lead_sponsor: Centre Mohammed VI de la Recherche et de l'Innovation (CM6RI)
primary_outcomes: The accuracy of a machine-learning based algorithm to predict high risk CKD from digital retinal images
title: Machine-learning Algorithm for Prediction of CKD From Retinal Images

brief_summary: The purpose of this prospective, non-therapeutic study is to evaluate molecular and clinical factors associated with clinical outcomes following CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy and bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) therapies in patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (R/R NHL).
primary_outcomes: Number of participants who achieve complete remission (CR) following CAR-T therapy
title: Genomic Predictors of Response to CAR-T and BiTE Therapies in B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas

brief_summary:
This observational cross-sectional study aims to investigate the association of excessive gestational weight gain with intestinal barrier function, metabolic endotoxemia, systemic inflammation, vitamin D/VDR signaling, and insulin resistance in pregnant women with normal pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI).

The study includes 80 women with singleton pregnancies at ≥37 weeks of gestation, divided into two groups according to the 2009 Institute of Medicine (IOM) gestational weight gain recommendations: excessive gestational weight gain (n=40) and recommended gestational weight gain (n=40).

Serum levels of zonulin, intestinal fatty acid-binding protein (I-FABP), glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2), lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP), soluble CD14 (sCD14), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), vitamin D receptor (VDR), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D \[25(OH)D\] will be evaluated. The findings may help identify biomarkers associated with maternal metabolic risk.
title: Gut Barrier Function and Metabolic Risk in Women With Excessive Gestational Weight Gain

brief_summary:
Lupus Nephritis (LN) is one of the most serious and common complications of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). It is a chronic inflammatory disease triggered by abnormal autoimmunity and the deposition of immune complexes in the kidneys. Approximately 40% to 60% of SLE patients develop lupus nephritis at the onset of the disease, and the cumulative rate of kidney involvement during the course of the disease can even reach 90%.

The goal of this Phase IIb, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial To Evaluate The Safety, Efficacy, And Pharmacokinetics Of IPG11406 Tablets In Participants With Lupus Nephritis trial is to evaluate the efficacy ，safety and tolerability of different doses of IPG11406 tablets combined with standard treatment compared to placebo combined with standard treatment in participants with active lupus nephritis.

A total of 4 groups were designed the 10mg IPG11406 tablet group, the 20mg IPG11406 tablet group, the 40mg IPG11406 tablet group,and the placebo group. The ratio among the groups was 1:1:1:1. Participants were randomly assigned to the above 4 dosage groups, with 48 participants planned for each group, totaling approximately 192 participants enrolled.

After randomization, participants will receive a 24-week double-blind treatment, twice daily (BID).They will take the assigned study drug (IPG11406 tablets at 40mg, 20mg, 10mg or placebo) orally.Throughout the 24-week core treatment period, all participants in all groups should continue to receive the standard treatment as prescribed by the protocol.

The primary efficacy endpoint of the renal response will be determined by changes in proteinuria and renal function. For the renal function assessment in the study visits, the glomerular filtration rate will be estimated using the CKD-EPI formula; proteinuria will be evaluated using the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (based on the 24-hour urine collected).
primary_outcomes: The proportion of participants who achieved complete renal remission (Completerenalresponse, CRR) at the 24th week.
title: A Study of IPG11406 Tablets in Participants With Lupus Nephritis

brief_summary:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic disease that causes inflammation and scarring of the bile ducts and can lead to progressive liver damage. There are currently no approved medications that have been shown to improve long-term outcomes in patients with PSC.

The purpose of this pilot study is to evaluate whether N-acetylcysteine (NAC), a medication that helps the body produce an antioxidant called glutathione, may improve liver blood tests in people with PSC.

This is a single-center, open-label study involving approximately 15 adults with PSC. All participants will receive oral NAC at a dose of 1,200 mg per day for the first 12 weeks. At Week 12, the dose will either remain the same or increase to 1,800 mg per day, depending on changes in a liver blood test called alkaline phosphatase (ALP).

Participants will continue treatment through Week 16. Those with a substantial improvement in ALP may be eligible to continue treatment through Week 20.

Researchers will evaluate changes in liver blood tests, treatment safety, side effects, and medication adherence. Additional blood tests may help researchers better understand how NAC affects liver injury.

This study is intended to provide preliminary information about the potential benefits and safety of NAC in PSC. It is not designed to establish whether NAC is an effective treatment for PSC.
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in Serum Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
title: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC)

brief_summary: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a psychiatric disorder characterized by recurrent intrusive obsessive thoughts, urges, and ritualized compulsive behaviors. OCD often follows a chronic and protracted course with a high risk of relapse and is frequently accompanied by comorbid anxiety, depression, and other negative emotional symptoms, resulting in substantial impairment in occupational functioning, interpersonal relationships, and family and social functioning.Integrative treatment combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Western medicine may help address several limitations of conventional monotherapy, including suboptimal treatment response rates, medication-related adverse effects, the limited diversity of available therapeutic approaches, and insufficiently individualized treatment strategies, thereby offering potential clinical benefits.Chaixia Dingzhi Powder, the investigational Chinese herbal formula used in this study, was developed based on the formulation principles of two classical TCM prescriptions, Xiaoyao San (Free and Easy Wanderer Powder), documented in the Taiping Huimin Heji Jufang (Formulary of the Pharmacy Service for Benefiting the People in the Taiping Era), and Banxia Houpo Tang (Pinellia and Magnolia Bark Decoction), recorded in the Jingui Yaolue (Essentials from the Golden Cabinet). The formula was further modified according to the TCM pathophysiological characteristics of the target population, particularly liver qi stagnation with spleen deficiency, impaired qi movement, and the interaction of phlegm and qi stagnation.Therefore, this study aims to further investigate the efficacy and safety of Chaixia Dingzhi Powder as an adjunctive traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) who have demonstrated nonresponse to initial SSRI treatment, while maintaining their existing SSRI therapy at an adequate therapeutic dose or the maximum tolerated dose.
title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Augmentation Therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

brief_summary:
Background Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) effectively relieves end-stage knee osteoarthritis, yet moderate-to-severe postoperative pain substantially compromises early functional exercise and rehabilitation. Liposomal bupivacaine, with a duration of action of up to 72 hours, offers a means of extending the postoperative pain-free window. However, previous studies have been limited by non-standardized background analgesia, absent head-to-head comparison of block targets, reliance on short-term resting pain scores, and inadequate blinding. Consequently, both the added value of liposomal bupivacaine nerve block on top of intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV-PCA) plus local infiltration analgesia (LIA), and the optimal block target, remain unresolved.

Objective To determine the analgesic added value of a single-shot liposomal bupivacaine targeted nerve block superimposed on standardized multimodal analgesia, and to compare the analgesic and functional recovery profiles of alternative block targets, thereby informing an optimized perioperative analgesic strategy.

Methods In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, three-arm controlled trial, 〔n〕 patients scheduled for unilateral TKA will be randomized to 〔arms to be confirmed: (1) background analgesia alone; (2) adductor canal block (ACB); (3) ACB combined with IPACK block〕. All patients receive standardized background analgesia comprising IV-PCA and intraoperative LIA. The primary endpoint is movement-evoked pain numeric rating scale (NRS) score at 〔24〕 h postoperatively. Secondary endpoints include resting pain scores, cumulative opioid consumption, time to first ambulation, knee range of motion, incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), and length of hospital stay.
lead_sponsor: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients Achieving Pain-Free Rehabilitation Within 72 Hours After Surgery (Composite)
title: Liposomal Bupivacaine Nerve Block for Knee Replacement Pain: Added Value and Optimization

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the effectiveness of ultrasound-guided Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) block and epidural block for postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing elective unilateral total hip arthroplasty. A total of 62 eligible patients will be randomly allocated into two groups: Group A will receive epidural block, and Group B will receive PENG block. Postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, time to first rescue analgesia, motor blockade, adverse effects, and time to mobilization will be assessed to compare the analgesic efficacy and recovery outcomes of the two techniques.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain score at rest and on movement using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
title: PENG Block Versus Epidural Block for Postoperative Analgesia After Total Hip Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether a multi-ingredient creatine supplement produces different effects on exercise performance, cognitive function, hydration, and gastrointestinal symptoms compared with creatine monohydrate alone.

Approximately 16 healthy, physically active adults aged 18-40 years will participate. Each participant will take creatine monohydrate (5 grams per day) for 18 days and a multi-ingredient supplement containing creatine monohydrate (5 grams), sodium, potassium, magnesium, and taurine for another 18 days. The order of supplementation will be randomly assigned, with a 30-day break between conditions.

Participants will complete laboratory testing before and after each supplementation period. Testing will include bench press exercise to assess muscular endurance, repeated high-intensity cycling tests to assess exercise performance, and a computerized cognitive task to measure attention and reaction time. Researchers will also assess hydration, selected blood markers, perceived exertion, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

The findings may help determine whether adding electrolytes and taurine to creatine provides additional benefits or produces different physiological responses compared with creatine monohydrate alone.
primary_outcomes: Peak Power During Repeated Wingate Tests
Mean Power During Repeated Wingate Tests
Total Work During Repeated Wingate Tests
title: Effects of Creatine Formulations on Exercise and Cognitive Performance

brief_summary:
The ASAS Project (Active Streets Around Schools), Task 3, is a cluster randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate a school-mediated, teacher-training intervention. Grounded in the bioecological model, the study's primary objective is to reduce parental fears regarding independent mobility and to increase active commuting to school among children in the 3rd to 6th grades, which corresponds to ages 8 to 12 years old.

The study will recruit 328 children and their respective parents across 13 schools (clusters), primarily within the Lisbon metropolitan area. This sample size accounts for a potential 30% dropout rate to ensure a minimum of 252 children complete the trial, divided by 6 clusters under the intervention (teacher training), and 7 clusters as the control group. The intervention focuses on training teachers to integrate active mobility concepts through continuous educational stimuli and interactive extracurricular challenges. This approach aims to strengthen the mesosystem between schools and families to reshape risk perception and build collective safety.

Participant evaluations will be conducted at baseline and five months post-intervention. The primary outcome is the 24-hour movement behaviors (physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep) assessed objectively via accelerometers. Secondary outcomes include the change in parental fears concerning children's independent mobility, measured using the Parental Fears and Fear of Strangers scales, which will undergo cross-cultural validation during the baseline data collection phase, the granting of independent mobility licenses by parents, and changes in the mode of school commuting. Additionally, the study will measure children's environmental literacy, and well-being using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). The final statistical analysis will utilize an intention-to-treat approach and mixed linear models to properly account for the hierarchical structure of the school cluster data.

The present study will enable teachers to act as key catalysts by integrating active travel, environmental literacy, and road safety concepts directly into school health practices. By fostering school-family collaboration, it will enable parents and local communities to reshape their risk perceptions and mitigate safety concerns regarding independent travel. This creates a supportive, enabling environment that empowers 3rd to 6th-grade children with critical road safety skills and spatial literacy, enabling them to receive independent mobility licenses, increase daily physical activity, and establish healthy, autonomous commuting habits over the long term.
title: TEACHING FOR ACTIVE TRAVEL

brief_summary: This Phase 1 study is designed to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety of a single oral dose of DA-302168S in subjects with moderate renal impairment (with the possible inclusion of subjects with mild renal impairment), compared with age-, sex-, and body mass index (BMI)-matched subjects with normal renal function. The results of this study will provide scientific evidence to support appropriate clinical dosing recommendations for DA-302168S in subjects with renal impairment.

brief_summary:
This study was conducted to examine the effects of a painting-based art intervention on social isolation, psychological recovery, and happiness levels in individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia, as well as to investigate the indirect effects of changes in social isolation and psychological recovery on the relationship between the intervention and changes in happiness.

The study employed a randomized controlled, parallel-group, pre-test/post-test design. A total of 60 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n=30) or a control group (n=30). The experimental group received a structured painting-based art intervention consisting of eight one-hour sessions over approximately two months. The control group did not receive the painting-based art intervention.

Data were collected before and after the intervention period using a personal information form, the Hikikomori Social Isolation Scale, the Mental Health Recovery Scale, and the Oxford Happiness Questionnaire-Short Form. Mixed-design analysis of variance was used to evaluate group-by-time interactions, and bootstrap analyses were conducted to examine indirect effects.
title: Effects of Painting-Based Art Interventions in Individuals With Schizophrenia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether sotatercept, an FDA-approved medication for people with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), can improve health outcomes for people with PAH due to use of methamphetamine. The main question it aims to answer is whether sotatercept added to standard background therapy and addiction medicine services will improve treatment response as measured by:

* Echocardiographic measurements of pulmonary hypertension
* Change in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD)
* Change in categorization of disease (World Health Organization Functional Class, WHO FC)
* Quality of life improvements

Participants will need to adhere to their standard PAH therapy as well as the prescribed sotatercept, as well as actively engaging with addiction medicine services. They will complete the following activities:

* Physical exam
* Labs including drug screening
* Pulmonary function testing (PFT)
* Exercise testing (6MWD)
* Echocardiography
* Right heart catheterization (RHC)
* Questionnaires related to their disease

Participants will be in the study for about six months.
title: Sotatercept in the Treatment of Methamphetamine-Associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

brief_summary:
Radiotherapy is thought to trigger an immune response, and the particular type of immune response may depend on the biology of individual tumours. By studying changes in the immune response and tumour biology during and after radiotherapy, we will gain a better understanding of how different types of radiotherapy, and different tumour types, affect the immune response. This is important for optimising personalised radiotherapy treatment, including in combination with other immunotherapy agents. There is minimal published data reporting feasibility of the above approach, or to guide power calculations. This means pilot work is needed to establish both feasibility and proof-of principle.

The CHIMERA protocol is a non-interventional single site study involving sample collection (blood and tumour samples) from patients before, during and after radiotherapy. A maximum of four tumour research biopsies are further optional research samples. The primary and secondary objectives of the CHIMERA protocol are to establish feasibility of longitudinal characterisation of firstly the immune response, and secondly tumour biology before, during and after radiotherapy.

Any patient receiving radiotherapy at The Royal Marsden NHS Trust is eligible for CHIMERA provided they are able to provide informed consent, attend follow up appointments and do not have an immunosuppressive infection.

If feasibility criteria are met for profiling of the immune response and tumour, CHIMERA will provide both preliminary data and proof-of-principle for larger studies in single tumour sites. CHIMERA is sponsored by the Institute of Cancer Research, LONDON. Funding is also provided by the Institute of Cancer Research.
conditions: Impact of the Immune Cell Repertoire on the Therapeutic Index of Radiotherapy
The Need for Serum Markers of Radiotherapy Toxicity
Measurement of Circulating Tumour DNA (ctDNA) During Radiotherapy
primary_outcomes: The feasibility of measuring the change in immune cell repertoire before, during and after radiotherapy
title: Characterisation of Immunological and Molecular Changes Evolving in Patients Undergoing Radiotherapy (CHIMERA)

brief_summary: This study aims to understand how people's physical abilities change during the first year after they leave specialist rehabilitation following a Spinal Cord Injury (SCI). It looks at how well people can move, care for themselves, and function in everyday life once they return to living in the community. We want to investigate whether people improve, stay the same, or experience a decline in their physical function over the first 12 months after in-patient rehabilitation. This information will help identify whether additional support or changes in care are needed after discharge from rehabilitation services. Specifically, we aim to recruit 80 people with SCI to explore physical function at three-time points, before discharge, and at 6 and 12 months post discharge from specialist SCI centres. We will also explore relationships between function, Physical Activity (PA) and individual characteristics.
primary_outcomes: Spinal Cord Independence Measure III Self-Report (SCIM III-SR)
title: Tracking Function in SCI

brief_summary:
Children of parents with a mental illness (COPMI) have an increased likelihood of developing mood disorders such as major depressive disorder or bipolar disorder. Especially adolescence is a particularly vulnerable time for the development of mood disorders. It is therefore important to intervene early to prevent the development of mood disorder symptoms and fully established mood disorders. This proposed MARIO online preventive intervention trial aims to examine the potential effects of access to an online platform (the MARIO preventive intervention platform), that integrates three preventive online interventions, on the development of mood disorder symptoms in COPMI. With a target sample size of N = 154 offspring - aged between 10 to 25 years - of parents with a mental illness, the researchers will conduct one of the largest Randomized Controlled Trials (RCT) for online preventive interventions in a high-risk offspring population to date. Participants in the experimental condition will receive 3 months access to the MARIO online preventive intervention platform through which participants can take part in up to 3 online preventive interventions for mood disorders. These intervention components include content targeted at COPMI specifically, including psychoeducation, social support, the implementation of adaptive coping strategies, and improving affective awareness. The preventive interventions will take between 4 and 8 weeks to complete. Outcome assessments take place in all participants at baseline (T0) and post-intervention (T1), as well as at 3-month (T2) and 9-month (T3) follow-up. Some outcomes are assessed at all time points, while others are only assessed at baseline (T0) and 9-month follow-up (T3).

The primary outcome measure are depression symptoms, assessed with the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) at post-intervention and at 3-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes include depressive symptoms at 9-month follow-up as well as bipolar mood disorder symptoms, psychosocial functioning, and usage of adaptive coping strategies across all time points. These secondary outcomes are also assessed using self-report questionnaires. The potential onset of a mood disorder is assessed as a secondary outcome using a clinical interview at 9-month follow-up. This interview is only conducted with participants who show significant mood disorder symptoms at any of the 4 time points, indicated by a PHQ-9 score of 5 and above.

With this RCT design, the researchers can assess if access to a platform with three online preventive interventions can help in preventing mood disorder symptoms in COPMI. This can deepen the understanding of vulnerabilities and needs for this high-risk population, which will hopefully contribute to improved long-term mental health outcomes.
conditions: Mood Disorders in Children and Adolescents
primary_outcomes: Development of depressive symptoms post-intervention and at 3-month follow-up
title: Preventing Mood Disorders in High-risk Offspring: Protocol for the Randomized Controlled Trial of the MARIO Online Preventive Intervention Platform

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether combining a beauty device with the test product affects skin parameters in women troubled by wrinkles. It aims to evaluate the impact of the beauty device on the efficacy of the test product. The main questions it aims to answer are:

\- Does the combination of the beauty device plus test product achieve better skin improvement compared with using the test product alone?

Researchers will compare beauty device + test product applied to one half of the face and one side of the neck against the test product alone applied to the contralateral half-face and neck, to see whether the beauty device enhances the efficacy of the test product.

Participants will:

* Receive randomized split-face and split-neck treatment during the study
* Attend 10 scheduled study visits
* Undergo standardized image capture, clinical assessment and instrumental skin measurement
interventions: Beauty device combined with test skincare product
primary_outcomes: Dermatologist clinical assessment of skin parameters using modified Griffiths 10-point scale
title: Device Impact on the Efficacy of Serum Product Study

brief_summary: This study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled single dose escalation (SAD) study conducted in patients with hyperuricemia with or without gout. The plan is to conduct ramp ups in 5 dose groups of 1mg, 2mg, 4mg, 6mg, and 8mg (adjustable during the study), with 8 subjects in each dose group and a total of 40 subjects. The sentinel method will be used for each dose group, with 2 subjects in the first group (1A+1P) followed by 6 subjects in the second group (5A+1P), to observe safety and tolerability.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Event and Serious Adverse Events
title: Safety and Tolerability of F012 in Patients With Hyperuricemia and Gout

brief_summary:
Overweight and obesity are increasingly common in adolescents. Italy, and in particular the Campania region, has one of the highest rates of excess weight in children and adolescents in Europe. Dietary approaches that are effective, safe and realistic for teenagers are needed.

This randomized controlled trial will compare two dietary programs with usual diet in adolescents aged 14 to 18 years with overweight or obesity. The study will test whether the Mediterranean Longevity Diet (MLD) and the Fasting Mimicking Diet (FMD) reduce body mass index (BMI) z-score more than continuing the usual diet, while preserving lean mass and normal growth.

The MLD is based on the traditional Mediterranean diet and adapted to the needs of adolescents. It is rich in vegetables, legumes, whole grains, fish, nuts and olive oil, with limited starchy and sugary foods, limited red meat, poultry, eggs and dairy, a moderate protein intake, and all food eaten within a 12-hour window each day. The FMD is a plant-based, low-calorie 5-day meal program that provides vitamins, minerals and essential fatty acids. It is repeated every 3 months, with the usual diet followed between cycles.

A total of 330 adolescents will be randomly assigned in equal numbers (110 per group) to one of three groups: (1) continuing the usual diet and lifestyle (control group), (2) the MLD for 12 months, or (3) the FMD, one 5-day cycle every 3 months, for 12 months. Participants in the control group may choose to follow the MLD or the FMD for 6 months after the first 6 months of the study.

Participants will attend three clinic visits (start of the study, 6 months and 12 months) and will be contacted every month by a nutritionist. At the visits, the research team will measure height, weight, body circumferences, blood pressure and body composition (bioelectrical impedance analysis), collect fasting blood samples and administer questionnaires on diet, lifestyle and sleep. Optional assessments include liver stiffness measurement (FibroScan), pubertal stage assessment, sleep monitoring with a wearable ring, and psychological support sessions.

The main outcome is the change in BMI z-score. Other outcomes include changes in fat mass, lean mass, waist circumference, blood pressure, blood lipids, glucose, HbA1c, insulin resistance, inflammation markers, liver fat index, sleep and diet quality. Safety is closely monitored, with rules for stopping the diet in case of rapid weight loss, fainting, low blood glucose, abnormal blood salts, or signs of eating disorders.

The study is conducted at the Evangelical Hospital Betania in Naples, Italy, in collaboration with the Valter Longo Foundation (Milan) and other clinical centers in Campania.
primary_outcomes: Change in BMI z-score from baseline to end of study
title: Mediterranean Longevity Diet and Fasting Mimicking Diet in Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary:
The goal of this exploratory study is to compare the immediate effects of rehabilitative ultrasound imaging (RUSI) feedback and manual feedback on serratus anterior muscle thickness during a shoulder exercise in adults with persistent rotator cuff-related shoulder pain.

The main question is whether RUSI feedback produces a greater percentage increase in serratus anterior muscle thickness than manual feedback.

Researchers compared two feedback conditions:

* \*\*RUSI feedback:\*\* Participants viewed real-time ultrasound images of their serratus anterior muscle while performing a shoulder exercise.
* \*\*Manual feedback:\*\* A physiotherapist provided tactile guidance and verbal instructions during the same exercise.

All participants performed both conditions in a randomly assigned order during a single session, with a 30-minute rest period between conditions.

Researchers measured serratus anterior muscle thickness using ultrasound at rest and during a standardized muscle contraction after each feedback condition. The measurements were used to compare the percentage increase in muscle thickness between the two feedback methods.
primary_outcomes: Between-Condition Difference in Percentage Increase in Serratus Anterior Muscle Thickness
title: Ultrasound and Manual Feedback for Serratus Anterior Muscle Activation in People With Shoulder Pain

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether structured supportive communication provided by the obstetric surgeon during elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia reduces maternal physical discomfort, pain, and anxiety compared with standard clinical communication.

Approximately 400 pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean delivery will be included in this prospective, non-randomized, controlled study at Kayseri City Hospital, Türkiye.

Six obstetric surgeons will participate in both communication groups. In the structured therapeutic communication group, surgeons will provide planned information, emotional support, and brief reassuring conversation at four stages of surgery. In the standard communication group, surgeons will continue routine clinical communication and respond to patients' questions and needs.

The communication approach will be assigned according to a pre-established operating-session schedule without randomization. Routine anesthesia, surgical care, and pain management will not be restricted by the study.

An independent observer will assess maternal pain, physical discomfort, and anxiety using numerical rating scales at four predefined surgical stages. The primary outcome will be the highest physical discomfort score recorded during the three intraoperative stages after surgical incision.

Additional outcomes will include intraoperative pain and anxiety, conversion to general anesthesia, postoperative pain, analgesic requirements, maternal recovery quality, and patient satisfaction. Postoperative assessments will be performed approximately 24 hours after delivery.
title: Surgeon-Led Therapeutic Communication During Elective Cesarean Delivery Under Spinal Anesthesia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether probiotics isolated from breast milk and healthy infant feces can reduce the severity of atopic dermatitis (eczema) in children aged 3 to 18 years with moderate-to-severe disease. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does taking the probiotic capsule twice daily for 12 weeks reduce eczema severity, measured by the EASI SCORAD?
* Does the probiotic improve quality of life, blood markers of allergic inflammation (IgE, histamine, IL-31, T-cell subsets), and gut microbiota composition? Researchers will compare the probiotic to a placebo capsule that looks the same but contains no probiotic bacteria.

Participants will:

* Take one capsule twice daily for 12 weeks, in addition to their usual atopic dermatitis treatment
* Complete the PO-SCORAD and a quality-of-life questionnaire at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 8 and 12
* Provide stool samples at baseline and weeks 4 and 12, and a 10 mL blood sample at baseline and week 12.
primary_outcomes: Change in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score from baseline to week 12
Change in white blood cell count
Change in absolute CD3+ T-cell count
Change in absolute CD4+ helper T-cell count
Change in absolute CD8+ suppressor/cytotoxic T-cell count

brief_summary: The purpose of this research study is to identify biomarkers (measurable signs in the body like substances in blood or urine) of whole grain (WG) barley intake following an acute exposure in pharmacokinetics (how the body absorbs, processes, and gets rid of a substance or ingredient) feeding study. In this aim, investigators will conduct a randomized crossover acute pharmacokinetic study of barley. Investigators will then use a targeted metabolomics approach to identify the exposure markers of barley intake, further develop analytical methods to study its pharmacokinetics, build our in-house WG metabolite database, and use an untargeted metabolomics approach to investigate postprandial biomarkers of barley intake. At the completion of this study, our expectation is that investigators will identify barley phytochemicals and its metabolites as objective biomarkers of total and individual WGs that are commonly consumed by Americans.
lead_sponsor: North Carolina Agriculture & Technical State University
primary_outcomes: Changes From Baseline in Plasma and Urine Metabolite Concentrations Following Whole-Grain Product Intake

brief_summary:
This study will examine the safety, feasibility, and potential benefits of transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (scTS) combined with activity-based training in people with spinal cord injury.

The study will include 10 adults with chronic, incomplete spinal cord injury. Electrical stimulation will be delivered through electrodes placed on the skin over different regions of the spinal cord, while participants perform exercises involving the arms, hands, trunk, and legs.

Participants will undergo initial assessments, individualized stimulation mapping, and 80 training sessions, followed by final assessments. Researchers will evaluate changes in motor function, muscle activity, psychological well-being, autonomic function, and quality of life. Safety and tolerability will also be monitored throughout the study.
title: Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation for Motor Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury

brief_summary:
This study is a single-center, single-arm, prospective clinical study enrolling a total of 30 patients with advanced metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma who have failed or progressed after prior first-line immunotherapy or immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy.

After signing the informed consent form, subjects will undergo screening assessment within 28 days prior to the first dose to determine whether they meet the study requirements. Subjects who meet the study inclusion and exclusion criteria will receive sacituzumab tirumotecan and a PD-1 inhibitor.

Patients will receive sacituzumab tirumotecan (4 mg/kg IV d1 Q2W) in combination with a PD-1 inhibitor for 6 cycles, followed by maintenance therapy with a PD-1 inhibitor-based regimen.

until investigator-confirmed radiological disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, the subject's request to discontinue treatment, or other protocol-specified criteria for treatment discontinuation, whichever occurs first; Eligible subjects will undergo regular tumor assessments based on RECIST 1.1. Within 48 weeks (within the first year) after dosing, imaging examinations for tumor assessment will be performed every 6 weeks (±7 days); after 48 weeks, tumor assessment will be performed every 12 weeks (±7 days), until radiological disease progression, initiation of new anti-tumor therapy, withdrawal of informed consent by the subject, loss to follow-up, death, or termination of the study by the sponsor, whichever occurs first. Imaging examinations will be performed as scheduled regardless of dose delay or adjustment. After a patient first achieves complete response (CR) or partial response (PR), the observed response must be confirmed at least 4 weeks (28 days) later.

For subjects who discontinue treatment for reasons other than radiological disease progression, death or loss to follow-up, imaging examinations should be repeated at the EOT visit if more than 4 weeks have elapsed since the previous imaging examination; subsequent imaging examinations should be performed as scheduled as far as possible until radiological disease progression, initiation of new anti-tumor therapy, withdrawal of informed consent by the subject, loss to follow-up, death, or termination of the study by the sponsor, whichever occurs first.

After the end of treatment, regardless of whether a new anti-tumor therapy is initiated, safety follow-up must be completed for the subject, and survival follow-up visits will be continued by telephone every 3 months (±14 days) after the last dose of study treatment to obtain survival information and information on new anti-tumor therapy, until the subject decides to withdraw from the study, loss to follow-up, death, or the end of the study, whichever occurs first.
lead_sponsor: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
title: A Single-Arm Phase II Clinical Study of Sacituzumab Tirumotecan Combined With a PD-1 Inhibitor as Second-Line Therapy for Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma After Failure of or Progression on Immunotherapy

brief_summary: This study included 100 patients with persistent AF, heart failure (left ventricular ejection fraction 30-60%), and iron deficiency who underwent successful electrical cardioversion. Fifty patients received 1000 mg intravenous FCM immediately before cardioversion, while 50 served as controls. The primary endpoint was AF recurrence within 12 months.
title: Association Between Intravenous Ferric Carboxymaltose Before Electrical Cardioversion and One-Year Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence in Patients With Heart Failure and Iron Deficiency

brief_summary: Inadequate management of pain during vaccination may lead to negative vaccination experiences, needle fear, and future vaccine non-adherence in children. This study aims to develop a web-based pain management education program for nurses/midwives and parents to reduce vaccination-related pain in children and evaluate its effectiveness. The study will be conducted using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with a non-randomized control group in two Family Health Centers. Pain will be assessed using the FLACC Pain Scale for children aged 0-3 years and the Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale for children aged 3 years and older. Pain management practices will be evaluated using an observation form. The information quality of the program will be assessed using DISCERN, and its usability will be evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS). Data will be analyzed using appropriate parametric and non-parametric tests. The intervention effect will be evaluated by examining the group-by-time interaction. Statistical significance will be set at p\<0.05.
primary_outcomes: Evidence-Based Pain Management Practices by Nurses/Midwives
Evidence-Based Pain Management Practices by Parents
Vaccination-Related Pain Scores in Children Aged 0-Under 3 Years
Vaccination-Related Pain Scores in Children Aged 3 Years and Older
title: Web-Based Training for Pain Management

brief_summary:
Only 2 out of 10 individuals meet the recommended dairy intake. This may be partly attributed to the high prevalence of lactose intolerance, which has led to an increased demand for lactose-free products. However, lactose-free milk contains high levels of its constituent monosaccharides (glucose and galactose), which increase its glycemic index (GI). GI is a key parameter in the dietary management of individuals with type 1 diabetes (T1D), as it helps guide food selection to achieve better glycemic control.

Emerging types of milk available on the market, such as goat and donkey milk, are naturally low in lactose and may represent lower-GI alternatives to lactose-free cow's milk. However, neither their GI nor their glycemic response in individuals with T1D has been evaluated.

Objective: To compare the GI in healthy individuals and the glycemic response in individuals with T1D following the consumption of donkey, goat, and cow's milk, with and without lactose.

Hypothesis: Donkey and goat milk have a lower GI in healthy individuals and elicit a lower glycemic response in individuals with T1D compared with regular and lactose-free cow's milk.

Methods: The GI in healthy individuals and the glycemic response in individuals with T1D will be determined following the consumption of regular cow's milk, lactose-free cow's milk, goat milk, and donkey milk, according to ISO 26642:2010. Each milk sample will provide 25 g of available carbohydrates and will be compared with a reference food (glucose solution).

Expected Results: Emerging types of milk are expected to have a lower GI than lactose-free cow's milk. Additionally, goat and donkey milk consumption is expected to result in a lower glycemic response than lactose-free cow's milk in individuals with T1D.
interventions: Milk Consumption (Cow's, Lactose-Free Cow's, Goat's, and Donkey's Milk).
title: Difference in Postprandial Blood Glucose Levels Following the Consumption of Isoglucidic Amounts of Milk With Different Lactose Contents in Individuals With Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the acute effects of different post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) strategies on agility and explosive performance in male kickboxers. Twenty trained male kickboxers will participate in a single-group, repeated-measures experimental study involving four conditions: plyometric jumps (PLY), heavy squats (HS), isometric squats (ISO), and control (CON). The effects of these conditions will be evaluated using countermovement jump (CMJ) height, relative peak power, and the Illinois Agility Test. All four conditions will be performed in a randomized order, with a minimum washout period of 72 hours between sessions.
title: Pape Strategies and Performance in Male Kickboxers

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of a four-week Tabata-style core endurance training programme on core muscle endurance and dynamic balance in female futsal players.

Thirty female futsal players aged 18-35 years participated in this randomized, parallel-group, single-blind study. Participants were randomly allocated to one of two groups: an intervention group (15 participants) and a control group (15 participants).

The intervention group performed a specific core endurance training programme consisting of isometric exercises, including front plank, right and left side plank, and reverse plank exercises. The programme lasted four weeks, with three sessions per week and approximately 20 minutes per session, in addition to the participants' usual futsal training. The control group continued their usual futsal training without the additional core training programme.

Core muscle endurance and dynamic balance were assessed before and after the intervention. Core endurance was evaluated using the Sport-Specific Endurance Plank Test (SSEPT), while dynamic balance was assessed using the Y Balance Test (YBT), which measures reach performance in the anterior, posteromedial, and posterolateral directions.

The study aims to determine whether adding a structured core endurance training programme to usual futsal training produces changes in core endurance and dynamic balance in female futsal players.
primary_outcomes: Core endurance measured by the Sport-Specific Endurance Plank Test (SSEPT)
title: Core Training and Dynamic Balance in Female Futsal Players

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the immediate effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) on voice characteristics and autonomic function in healthy adults.

A total of 36 healthy adults aged 18-30 years will participate in this randomized, sham-controlled, three-period crossover trial. Each participant will receive three interventions in a randomized order: unilateral active taVNS, bilateral active taVNS, and sham stimulation. Each intervention will last 20 minutes, with at least seven days between visits.

Voice characteristics will be evaluated before and after each intervention using acoustic analysis. The primary outcome will be shimmer, a measure of variation in voice amplitude. Secondary outcomes will include jitter, harmonics-to-noise ratio, and fundamental frequency. Perceived vocal effort, heart rate, and pulse rate variability will also be assessed.

The study will compare the immediate effects of unilateral, bilateral, and sham stimulation on voice stability and explore possible relationships between voice changes and autonomic responses.
title: Effects of Unilateral and Bilateral Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Voice Acoustics in Healthy Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to learn whether an ultrashort echo time (UTE) MRI scan can show the position of brachytherapy applicators and needles more accurately than standard MRI scans in adults with gynaecologic cancer (cervical, endometrial, or vaginal cancer) who are receiving MRI-guided internal radiotherapy (brachytherapy).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does UTE MRI locate the applicator and needle tips more accurately than standard T2-weighted (T2W) and proton-density-weighted (PDW) MRI, when compared with CT?
* Does UTE MRI show a clearer contrast between the applicator and the surrounding tissue?

Researchers will compare applicator positions reconstructed from UTE, T2W, and PDW MRI with CT taken on the same day as the reference standard. They will also check whether differences in applicator reconstruction change the planned radiation dose, and whether image features (radiomics) from UTE MRI before treatment and before brachytherapy help predict cancer recurrence.

Participants will:

* Receive their usual standard brachytherapy treatment, which is not changed by this study
* Have one additional MRI sequence (UTE, about 8 minutes) added to their standard MRI and CT scans at each brachytherapy planning session, with the applicator in place
* Have an additional UTE sequence added to their routine MRI before treatment and before brachytherapy
* Be followed during routine clinical visits for disease outcomes
title: Ultrashort Echo Time (UTE) MRI for Applicator Reconstruction in Gynaecologic Cancer Brachytherapy

brief_summary:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic joint disease that develops when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own joints. The small joints of the hands and feet are most commonly affected, resulting in joint pain, swelling, and tenderness. Over time, permanent joint damage may occur, making it difficult for individuals to perform their daily activities. Rheumatoid arthritis may affect not only the joints but also other organs, such as the heart and lungs, in some individuals. Therefore, it is considered a health condition that can affect multiple body systems. It is more common in women than in men and is the most prevalent inflammatory joint disease among adults.

Rheumatoid arthritis is highly prevalent worldwide, affecting approximately 0.5-1% of the population. According to the 2021 Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, approximately 17.6 million people worldwide were living with rheumatoid arthritis in 2020, and the prevalence of the disease has increased substantially since 1990.

In the early stages of the disease, symptoms are generally mild and nonspecific. Individuals may experience fatigue, weakness, and loss of appetite, along with joint pain. Diagnosis can be challenging during this period. As the disease progresses, characteristic clinical manifestations become more pronounced, and joint involvement typically develops symmetrically, particularly affecting the joints of the hands, wrists, knees, and feet.

The exact cause of rheumatoid arthritis remains unknown. However, research suggests that genetic predisposition, hormonal factors, and environmental factors may contribute to its development. The disease can adversely affect not only physical health but also psychological well-being and quality of life, requiring patients to make changes to their daily routines and lifestyle habits.
primary_outcomes: The Richard Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) Score
title: The Effects of Su Jok Therapy in Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary:
Healthy aging is characterized by impaired spatial memory compared to younger adults. These impairments not only negatively impact quality of life but are also an early marker for the onset of dementia, especially Alzheimer's Disease. While sleep plays an active role in spatial memory consolidation in young adults, the extent to which sleep contributes to this process in aged adults is yet to be determined. The objective of this developmental R21 project is to determine the impact of sleep on spatial memory in cognitively healthy, aged adults, and evaluate the potential for a sleep intervention targeting memory reactivation to improve performance in this population. The project will include a single experiment using an ecologically valid ambulatory virtual environment to test the effects of sleep on spatial memory performance in aged adults.

Aim 1 will determine whether post-learning sleep benefits spatial memory in aged adults, more so than a period of wakefulness. Spatial memory performance will be measured using well-established tasks in a virtual environment, before and after a 90-minute delay consisting of either an EEG-monitored nap or wakefulness. Changes in performance between these two conditions will be measured after the 90-minute delay and again one week later. The key hypothesis for this aim is that post-learning sleep will improve spatial memory recall more than an equivalent period of wakefulness, and that this improvement will correlate with sleep stages and EEG waveforms that are linked with memory consolidation.

Aim 2 will test whether targeted memory reactivation, a technique used to bias memory consolidation by obtrusively presenting sounds during sleep, can be used to enhance spatial memory in aged adults. To this end, task-related sounds will be presented to participants during a nap immediately after learning and during nocturnal sleep over the following week. Spatial memory performance will be compared between this group and a sleep group for which no sounds will be presented during sleep. The key hypotheses are that this manipulation will improve spatial memory performance, and that these behavioral effects will be mediated by memory-related EEG waveforms elicited by sounds presented during sleep.

By combining sleep, high-density electrophysiology, and a realistic testing environment, this project will determine the benefit of sleep on spatial memory in aged adults and test ways to leverage sleep to make consolidation more efficient. Results will inform our understanding of sleep-dependent consolidation in aged adults and pave the way for scalable, non-invasive treatments to improve day-to-day life and provide critical protections against dementia.
primary_outcomes: Performance on spatial memory task - wayfinding task
Performance on spatial memory task - pointing task
title: The Role of Sleep in Protecting Spatial Memories From Age-Related Decline

brief_summary: Opioid medications are a significant component of the management of chronic pain. Chronic use of opioids disrupts sleep architecture and cause respiratory depression, which is particularly prevalent during sleep. Chronic opioids induce sleep disordered breathing (SDB) including sleep hypoventilation, central sleep apnea and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). It was previously shown that oxytocin can treat SDB. There is emerging evidence that oxytocin can treat substance use disorder and has analgesic properties. Oxytocin efficacy of prevention of respiratory depression after acute opioid use will be examined as well as oxytocin efficacy in chronic opioid use.
title: OXytocin For Opioid Respiratory Depression

brief_summary:
Patients with cancer or chronic inflammatory disorders, such as periampullary malignancies or chronic pancreatitis (CP), often experience severe weight loss and a progressive decline in health and functional performance. These changes result from a complex interaction between the disease and the host, affecting multiple physiological factors. However, in daily clinical practice the focus is predominantly placed on treatment of the disorder itself, whereas less attention is given to the physical condition of the patient before treatment commences. Factors such as malnutrition, reduced aerobic fitness, and adverse body composition have all been associated with worse outcomes, including a higher risk of postoperative complications or inability to complete oncological treatment.

The central hypothesis of the investigators is that improving the patient's overall condition before treatment, particularly before major surgery, will enhance treatment tolerance, reduce complications, and improve overall quality of life (QoL). Among the various modifiable factors in the disease-host interaction, nutritional status occupies a central role, directly influencing muscle mass and strength, immune competence, metabolic stability, and recovery capacity.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grade IIIa or higher)
Preoperative energy coverage as a percentage of estimated energy requirement
Preoperative protein coverage as a percentage of estimated protein requirement
title: The imPAct of nutritioN on the Outcome of pancrEATic Surgery; Food for Thought.

brief_summary:
Heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, yet it often goes undetected until it's too late. This project uses a simple clue found during routine breast cancer screenings-breast arterial calcification (BAC)-to spot early signs of heart risk in women aged 50 to 70. Those identified with BAC will be invited to take part in a personalized prevention program. This includes support to adopt healthier habits-like being more active, eating better, sleeping well, and managing stress-and regular checks of key health measures such as blood pressure and cholesterol. The study will compare two levels of care: a nurse-led program and a more intensive, app-supported version.

By turning mammograms into a dual-purpose tool for breast and heart health, this project empowers women with early action to reduce risk and improve long-term well-being.
interventions: Digital Cardiovascular Health Education and Personalized Physical Activity Program
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving cardiovascular risk control targets
title: Study on Integrating the Systematic Detection of Breast Arterial Calcifications (BAC) in Routine Mammograms Within a Population-based Breast Cancer Screening Programme to Improve Cardiovascular Prevention in Women.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to understand the prevalence of topical corticosteroid phobia and to identify if personalized behavior intervention method can reduce the score of topical corticosteroid phobia among parents or caregivers of children with atopic dermatitis. The aims of the study are:

* to describe the prevalence of topical corticosteroid phobia in Indonesia
* to identify risk factor of topical corticosteroid phobia among parents of children with atopic dermatitis
* to evaluate if the intervention of BERANI method will reduce the score of topical corticosteroid phobia
* to assess the impact of intervention to the compliance and clinical outcome

Researchers will compare BERANI method to a standard care to see if BERANI method will reduce the score of topical corticosteroid phobia.

Participants will:

* fill a questionnaire and undergo physical examination for assessing the severity of atopic dermatitis
* get an audiovisual education or standard care education during the first visit based on randomization
* return in 14 days to fill a questionnaire and undergo physical examination.

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized study is to evaluate the feasibility of electronic questionnaires for assessing health-related quality of life in adults with breast or prostate cancer undergoing radiotherapy.

The main questions are:

* Can electronic questionnaires be successfully used to collect quality-of-life information?
* Does the mode of questionnaire administration (electronic or paper-based) affect questionnaire completion rates?
* Do patients report their quality of life differently depending on whether they complete questionnaires electronically or on paper? The study compares electronic and paper-based questionnaire administration to assess differences in questionnaire completion and quality-of-life responses.

Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* Electronic group: Participants received questionnaires online and could complete them using a computer, tablet, or smartphone.
* Paper group: Participants received printed questionnaires provided by healthcare staff.

Both groups were asked to complete the same quality-of-life questionnaires at three time points: during radiotherapy planning, on the first day of radiotherapy, and on the last day of radiotherapy.
title: Quality of Life of Patients Treated by Radiotherapy for Breast and Prostate Carcinoma

brief_summary:
Patients with co-existent endometrial and ovarian carcinomas (CEOCs) are treated inconsistently due to a lack of clear standardized treatment guidelines. Patients may be over-treated and face substantial physical side effects and financial challenges due to additional chemotherapy or radiation appointments. Previous retrospective research has shown that using specific molecular and pathologic criteria to stratify patients' CEOC tumours can identify patients at very low risk of cancer recurrence (during an average 6 years of follow-up), with no demonstrated benefit of additional treatment after surgery.

The goal of this study is to determine the safety of receiving no additional treatment (i.e. no chemotherapy or radiation) after surgery in patients diagnosed with a co-existent endometrial and ovarian cancer (CEOC) meeting highly selective molecular and pathologic criteria. Patients with CEOC who also meet predefined molecular criteria (low risk POLEmut, ER+NSMP, or MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 loss without MLH1 promoter hypermethylation in the endometrium and ovary) and pathology criteria (see schema) are eligible to participate. Patients may choose, or be directed by their physician to receive no additional treatment after surgery or to receive additional treatment.

To determine the safety of this approach, the study team will evaluate pelvic recurrence (primary) rate, as well as vaginal and distant recurrences, recurrence-free and disease- specific, and overall survival, quality of life, and health economic metrics among patients who do, and do not receive additional treatment after surgery.

Study design is pragmatic, designed to match recommended standard of care as closely as possible. Patients will have regular follow-up appointments with their oncologist every 4 months for 3 years as part of their medical care. During this time, patients will complete quality of life surveys at baseline, 4, 12, 24, and 36 months. Baseline imaging, and imaging at completion of 3-years are required.
primary_outcomes: Pelvic recurrence rate of participants in the treatment de-escalation group
title: Co-Existent Endometrial and Ovarian Carcinoma: Molecular Stratification for Pathologic Reporting and Clinical Management

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to find out whether ultrasound can reliably detect dilatation and aneurysms of the aorta, the main blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body, in people with giant cell arteritis (GCA). GCA causes inflammation in the blood vessel walls. It can affect the aorta and increase the risk of aortic dilatation and aneurysms. Aortic dilatation is an abnormal widening of the aorta. When it becomes large, it is called an aneurysm, and can lead to serious complications.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

How accurately can ultrasound performed by rheumatologists detect dilatation and aneurysms of the aorta compared with computed tomography (CT) angiography, which provides detailed images of the aorta?

How consistently do different rheumatologists evaluate the aorta using ultrasound?

How often is aortic dilatation and aneurysms found in people with GCA who previously had signs of inflammation in the aorta on a PET-CT scan?

Researchers will compare ultrasound measurements with CT angiography findings to assess how well ultrasound detects aortic dilatation and aneurysms.

The study will include 102 participants: 82 people with GCA and previous signs of aortic inflammation on PET-CT, 10 people with GCA and a known aortic dilatation or aneurysm, and 10 people with aortic dilatation or aneurysm not caused by inflammation.

Participants will undergo an ultrasound examination of the ascending aorta, the part of the aorta closest to the heart. Participants will also undergo CT angiography of the aorta, which uses X-rays and contrast dye to produce detailed images of the blood vessel. The ultrasound measurements will be compared with the CT angiography findings. The ultrasound evaluations of the ultrasound performing rheumatologists will be compared with evaluations of a blinded assessor.

The long-term aim is to determine whether ultrasound could be a useful, non-invasive screening method to help identify aortic dilatation and aneurysms in people with GCA.
lead_sponsor: Esbjerg Hospital - University Hospital of Southern Denmark
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of thoracic aorta ultrasound for detecting aortic dilatation and aneurysms
title: Ultrasound Screening of the Aorta in Giant Cell Arteritis

brief_summary:
People with type 2 diabetes receive standard dietary advice to improve glycaemic control. However, blood glucose responses to the same foods can vary considerably between individuals. This randomised controlled trial aims to investigate whether personalised carbohydrate recommendations guided by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) improve glycaemic control (HbA1c) compared with standard dietary care.

A total of 130 adults with type 2 diabetes will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The study will include a 6-month intervention period followed by a 6-month follow-up period. The intervention group will receive dietitian-led personalised carbohydrate recommendations informed by CGM data, supplemented by group-based education in carbohydrate counting. The control group will receive standard individual dietary counselling provided by a dietitian without the use of CGM.

The primary outcome is the between-group difference in change in HbA1c from baseline to 6 months.
title: The PRECISE-DIET Trial
