brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of palm (hand point) pressure and LI4 (Hegu) acupressure applied during labor on labor pain, duration of labor, and maternal birth satisfaction. A total of 105 nulliparous women aged 18-35 years with a term, low-risk, singleton pregnancy in spontaneous labor will be randomly assigned to three groups of 35: a palm pressure group, an LI4 acupressure group, and a control group receiving routine labor care. In the palm group, women press a wooden comb into their own palm during contractions. In the LI4 group, the researcher applies pressure to the LI4 point during contractions using an Electronic Acupuncture Pen and Meridian Massage Device. Applications are performed during six contractions (about 15-20 minutes) at cervical dilatations of 4-5 cm, 6-7 cm and 8-10 cm. Pain is measured with a Visual Analog Scale and an observer-rated pain expression scale (ESVADOPA) before and 30 minutes after each application. Duration of labor and neonatal Apgar scores are recorded, and birth satisfaction is assessed within 4 hours after birth. The study is conducted in a single center in Gaziantep, Türkiye.
interventions: LI4 Acupressure with Electronic Acupuncture Pen and Meridian Massage Device
primary_outcomes: Labor pain intensity measured by Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Effect of Palm and LI4 (Hegu) Acupressure on Labor Pain, Labor Duration and Satisfaction

brief_summary:
Brief Summary The purpose of this observational study is to better understand how vitamin D levels affect the gut microbiome (the bacteria that live in the intestines) in children who are newly diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Researchers want to learn whether low vitamin D levels are linked to changes in gut bacteria and whether this may affect how children with ALL respond to chemotherapy.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Are the gut bacteria different in children with ALL who have low vitamin D levels compared to those with normal vitamin D levels at the time of diagnosis?
* How do vitamin D levels relate to changes in gut bacteria and related body processes before and after induction chemotherapy? Researchers will compare children who have low vitamin D levels with those who have normal vitamin D levels to see if there are differences in their gut bacteria and how those bacteria change during early treatment. The stool samples will be studied in specialized laboratories to better understand how vitamin D and gut bacteria interact.

The results of this study may help doctors understand whether monitoring and managing vitamin D levels could improve care and treatment outcomes for children with ALL.

Participants will:

Have four study visits:

* Screening: Review and sign consent/assent forms, review of Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria, medical history, and current medications
* At diagnosis (baseline): Review of medications, laboratory results, Vitamin D level, Fecal Sample Collection
* Day 29-32 - At the end of induction chemotherapy: Review of medications, laboratory results, Vitamin D level, Fecal Sample Collection and Adverse event assessment
* Day 90-97 after Induction: Review of medications, laboratory results, Vitamin D level, Fecal Sample Collection and Adverse event assessment
title: Impact of Vitamin D on Gut Microbiome and Metabolome Among Pediatric Oncology Patients

brief_summary: Peripheral intravenous cannulation is one of the most frequently performed invasive procedures in infants and can cause pain, physiological stress, and behavioral distress. The use of non-pharmacological methods is increasingly important to reduce negative experiences during the procedure. This research was planned to evaluate the effect of a rotating sensory toy and parental presence on pain and clinically relevant outcomes during peripheral intravenous cannulation in infants aged 1-24 months. The study will be conducted as a three-arm, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial in the Pediatric Ward of Bartın State Hospital. The sample will consist of a total of 150 infants who agree to participate and meet the inclusion criteria. Participants will be assigned to three groups using a computer-based block randomization method: a rotating sensory toy group, a parental presence group, and a control group. The primary outcome variable of the study is pain level, assessed using the FLACC Pain Scale. Secondary outcome variables are crying duration, heart rate, oxygen saturation, procedure time, successful intravenous access on the first attempt, and parental and nurse satisfaction. FLACC scores will be assessed by an independent pediatric nurse unaware of the investigator and group assignments to reduce observer bias. The findings of this study are expected to provide evidence for effective, safe, and low-cost non-pharmacological interventions that can be applied during peripheral intravenous cannulation and to contribute to pediatric nursing practice.
primary_outcomes: FLACC Pain Scale (Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability)
title: The Effects of Rotating Sensory Toys and Parental Presence During Peripheral Intravenous Cannulation in Infants

brief_summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about the effects of felzartamab, also known as BIIB148, in adult participants with generalized myasthenia gravis, also known as gMG. This is a type of autoimmune disease that affects the signals sent between nerve cells and the muscles. An autoimmune disease means the body's immune system attacks its own healthy cells.

In people with gMG, the body's immune system makes abnormal antibodies that affect the signals that can be sent between the muscle and the nerves at the neuromuscular junction. The neuromuscular junction is where the nerve and muscle connect. The most common antibodies made in gMG are those that target 1 of 2 types of proteins - AchR (acetylcholine receptor) and MuSK (muscle-specific tyrosine kinase).

In this study, researchers wanted to learn more about a study drug called felzartamab. Researchers think felzartamab may lower the amount of antibodies against AChR or MuSK and allow signals between muscles and nerves to be sent normally again.

The main goal of the study is to compare the effects of felzartamab to a placebo on symptoms and daily living activities in adult participants with gMG. A placebo looks like the study drug but does not contain any medicine.

The main question researchers want to answer is:

* Does felzartamab increase the ability to perform daily activities after 26 weeks of treatment in participants with AChR antibodies?

Researchers will also learn more about:

* How many participants have adverse events and serious adverse events during the study? Adverse events are health problems that may or may not be caused by the study drug.
* How the body processes felzartamab
* How felzartamab affects the participants' disease severity
* How many participants' bodies make antibodies against felzartamab after treatment

This study will be done as follows:

* Participants will join the study after signing an informed consent form, also known as an ICF.
* Participants will be screened to check if they can join the study. Participants will then be assigned to a study group based on the type of antibodies they have.

  * If participants have AChR antibodies, they will be randomly assigned to receive either felzartamab or a placebo. Neither the participants nor the researchers will know if participants are getting the study drug or the placebo.
  * If participants have MuSK antibodies, they will receive felzartamab. In this group, the participants, study doctor, and study staff know which drug the participant is taking.
* Both felzartamab and the placebo will be given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, which involves giving the drug into a vein.
* During the study, participants will have regular clinic visits and phone calls. At the visits, participants will have blood and urine samples taken and will also have their overall health checked. The participants will also be asked questions about how they are feeling and how their gMG is affecting their daily lives.
* After their last dose, participants will enter a follow-up safety period for more testing and monitoring of their health.
primary_outcomes: Cohort 1: Change From Baseline in Myasthenia Gravis-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) Total Score at Week 26
title: A Study to Learn About the Effects of Felzartamab on Daily Living Activities and Its Safety in Adults With Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG) Ages 18 to 80 Years Old

brief_summary:
Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common type of irregular heartbeat in adults. People with AF may also have other heart problems, including reduced heart pumping function or diseases affecting the heart muscle or heart valves. Identifying these problems early is important because the condition of the heart can affect treatment decisions and long-term care.

An ultrasound examination of the heart, called transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) or an echocardiogram, is commonly used to check how well the heart pumps blood and to look for structural problems, such as heart valve disease. However, an echocardiogram requires special equipment and trained healthcare professionals to perform and interpret the examination. Because of these requirements, it may not always be available when needed. This can be particularly challenging in situations where heart function needs to be evaluated quickly, such as when a patient with AF has a very fast heart rate. Delays may also occur in outpatient settings because of limited availability of echocardiography.

Artificial intelligence (AI) technology may provide an additional way to identify patients who are more likely to have heart problems and who may benefit from further evaluation. A standard 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is a simple and widely available test that records the electrical activity of the heart. AI-based computer programs can analyze information contained in an ECG that may not be easily recognized through routine interpretation.

This study will use two AI-based ECG programs, called AiTiALVSD and AiTiALVDD. AiTiALVSD analyzes a standard 12-lead ECG to identify patients who may have reduced heart pumping function. Previous studies have evaluated this program in different clinical settings, including patients with AF and a fast heart rate.

AiTiALVDD analyzes the ECG for signs that may be associated with difficulty in the heart relaxing and filling with blood. Problems with heart relaxation and filling may occur in several types of heart disease, including heart valve disease, abnormal thickening of the heart muscle, heart disease related to high blood pressure, diseases affecting the heart muscle, and coronary artery disease. Importantly, some patients may have these conditions even when the heart's overall pumping function is normal. Therefore, evaluating only pumping function may not identify all patients who have important underlying heart disease.

By using AiTiALVSD and AiTiALVDD together, this study aims to evaluate a broader AI-based approach to identifying heart problems in patients with AF. AiTiALVSD may help identify patients who are more likely to have reduced heart pumping function, while AiTiALVDD may provide additional information about possible problems with heart relaxation and filling. A high-risk result from AiTiALVDD may serve as a signal that further heart evaluation should be considered, including evaluation for significant heart valve disease or other underlying structural heart conditions.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether using these two AI-based ECG programs together can help identify patients with AF who may have previously unrecognized problems with heart function or underlying heart disease. Patients identified by the AI analysis as being at higher risk may receive further evaluation as appropriate to determine whether additional heart disease is present.

The study will also evaluate the clinical usefulness of this AI-based ECG approach in routine care. The goal is not to replace an echocardiogram or a physician's clinical assessment. Instead, AI-based ECG analysis may serve as an additional screening tool to help healthcare professionals identify patients who may benefit from further cardiac testing.

By using information from a routinely performed ECG, this approach may help support earlier and more efficient evaluation of heart function and underlying heart disease in patients with AF. The results of this study will help determine whether combining AiTiALVSD and AiTiALVDD can provide useful information for deciding which patients may need additional cardiac evaluation and whether this approach can improve the process of identifying clinically important heart conditions.
primary_outcomes: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite outcome
title: Artificial Intelligence-enabled Management of Atrial Fibrillation(ABLE-AF Trial)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the study drug QL1706 (iparomlimab and tuvonralimab injection) works to treat locally advanced pancreatic cancer in adults when it is given together with chemotherapy and Stereotactic radiotherapy. It will also learn about the safety of this combination treatment.

Around 37 adults aged 18 to 75 who have pancreatic cancer that has grown into nearby tissue and cannot be removed by surgery, but has not spread to other parts of the body, and who have not yet received any treatment for it, will take part in this study.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the combination of QL1706, chemotherapy and radiation make the tumor shrink or stop growing, making it suitable for surgery? How long do participants live without their cancer getting worse, and how long do they live overall? What medical problems do participants have when taking this combination treatment? All participants in this study will receive the same treatment. There is no placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) and no comparison group. Researchers will compare the results of participants in this study with the results usually seen in people who receive chemotherapy alone, to see if adding QL1706 and radiation helps.

Participants will:

Receive QL1706 through a vein (by intravenous infusion) once every 3 weeks Receive 2 chemotherapy drugs through a vein on days 1 and 8 of every 3-week cycle, for 2 cycles. The 2 drugs are gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel Then receive 5 doses of focused radiation therapy to the pancreas, given about every other day over about 2 weeks, together with 2 more cycles of QL1706 and chemotherapy. Participants whose cancer gets worse during treatment will stop this part of the study Have CT or MRI scans every 6 weeks so the researchers can see whether the cancer has shrunk Have blood tests, physical examinations and other checkups during treatment Be reviewed by a team of pancreatic cancer specialists to see if surgery to remove the tumor is possible. Participants who can have surgery will have the surgery and then 2 to 4 more cycles of QL1706 and chemotherapy. Participants who cannot have surgery, and whose cancer has not grown, will keep receiving QL1706 and chemotherapy until their cancer gets worse, the treatment becomes too hard to tolerate, or they are no longer able to take part Tell the study team about any medical problems they have, which will be recorded throughout the study.
title: Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab Injection （QL1706）Combined With Chemotherapy (AG) and SBRT as First-Line Treatment for Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary: This is a Phase 2/3, open-label, multicenter study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of GH56 as a single agent in participants with advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma(ESCC) with methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) deficiency in the second-line or later setting. In this seamlessly designed Phase 2/3 study, a single-arm Phase 2 study will be conducted first, and after favorable efficacy data are obtained, a Phase 3 study comparing against standard chemotherapy will then be conducted.
title: GH56 Monotherapy for Second-line Treatment of MTAP-Deleted ESCC

brief_summary:
Keloids are fibroproliferative pathological scars characterized by uncontrolled dermal fibroblast proliferation and excessive collagen deposition, typically triggered by skin trauma, recurrent acne, or folliculitis; clinically, they extend beyond the boundaries of the original injury, presenting as elevated, firm, hyperemic papules/nodules and often accompanied by pruritus. As a prevalent condition in dermatology and plastic surgery, keloid pathogenesis and progression are modulated by multifaceted factors (e.g., genetics, tissue tension, anatomical location, immune inflammation), with high-tension sites (e.g., chest, scapulae) associated with poor responses to conservative therapies and elevated recurrence rates.

Per the 2018 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Keloid Management in China, surgery combined with adjuvant radiotherapy is recommended for medium-to-large keloids (2.0-10.0 cm) to mitigate systemic adverse events associated with high-dose local-block therapy. Core excision-currently widely adopted for such lesions-involves resection of the dermal fibrous core while preserving the epidermal/papillary dermal flap to avoid additional incisions; however, it entails substantial trauma, cumbersome operation, and high recurrence when applied to clustered multiple keloids. Micro-punch excision combined with radiotherapy, pioneered by our department, offers minimal invasiveness and tension reduction, yet its efficacy and safety relative to core excision remain uninvestigated (no peer-reviewed literature has directly compared these two approaches for multiple keloids).

The present prospective, self-controlled clinical trial will be conducted in the Department of Dermatology at Xijing Hospital, spanning April 2025 to December 2026. Eligible participants are Han Chinese individuals (18-65 years) with histopathologically confirmed multiple keloids (≥2 lesions in a single anatomical region), meeting: (1) a Japanese Scar Scale (JSS) total score ≥6 or ≥2 individual JSS items (height, hardness, erythema, periscar flush, pain/tenderness, pruritus) scoring ≥2; (2) keloid diameter ≥2 cm, with ineffectiveness after ≥3 cycles of local-block therapy or post-treatment recurrence; (3) planned management with either micro-punch excision + electron beam radiotherapy or core excision + electron beam radiotherapy. Exclusion criteria include anesthesia allergies, systemic comorbidities (e.g., malignancy, immunodeficiency), neurological/psychiatric disorders precluding treatment adherence, pregnancy/lactation, poor follow-up compliance, and concurrent inflammatory skin diseases (e.g., psoriasis).

A total of 20 participants will be enrolled. For each participant, multiple keloids in the target anatomical region will be allocated to two study arms via stratified randomization:

Experimental Arm: Micro-punch excision (0.8-2.4 mm BFY-STE micro-punch, Shandong Shensi Medical Devices Co., Ltd.) under local anesthesia, with 1-mm interval extractions (to visual flatness, deep to the fat layer) followed by open wound pressure dressing; Control Arm: Core excision (incisions parallel to skin tension lines, resection of the fibrous core to the superficial fascia, with marginal scar preservation for tension-free closure) under local anesthesia, followed by subcutaneous 5-0 absorbable suture and pressure dressing.

Adjuvant electron beam radiotherapy (Varian 23EX linear accelerator, 4 MeV energy) will be administered to both arms within 24 hours post-surgery: 16 Gy total dose (4 Gy per session, 4 sessions every other day), with a 1-cm margin around lesions and 0.5-cm shielding film for adjacent normal skin.

Follow-up assessments will be performed at 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 months post-surgery. Primary endpoints will include the 6-month treatment response rate (defined as ≥30% reduction in Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale \[POSAS\] score vs. baseline) and 6-month POSAS score. Secondary endpoints will encompass the 12-month recurrence rate (defined as POSAS score ≥21), recurrence time, Antaro-3D skin imaging metrics (scar thickness, erythema intensity), JSS score changes, and adverse events (e.g., skin atrophy, pigmentation, vascular dilatation).

Severe adverse events (e.g., wound infection/dehiscence, radiation-induced hematological/hepatic/renal impairment) will trigger immediate study termination; routine monitoring (daily 7-day post-surgery follow-up for pain/temperature, blood routine/hepatic-renal function tests at 3/6 months) will be implemented to capture adverse events.

This study aims to compare the clinical outcomes and safety profiles of micro-punch excision vs. core excision (both combined with electron beam radiotherapy) for multiple keloids. Findings are anticipated to identify an optimal therapeutic strategy for multiple keloids and establish evidence-based support for the standardized application of micro-punch excision in clinical practice.
title: Comparative Analysis of Efficacy and Safety in Patients With Keloids Treated With Either Micro-punch Excision or Core Excision

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether AI-assisted dignity therapy can effectively enhance dignity and reduce depression among older adults in community integrated care centers and daycare centers, while also evaluating the feasibility. The research objectives are as follows:

1. To analyze the current status of dignity and depression among older adults in community integrated care centers and daycare centers.
2. To explore the correlation between the dignity and depression in older adults.
3. To develop and implement a community-based intervention model centered on dignity therapy, utilizing artificial intelligence as an supportive tool, and to assess its feasibility.
4. To examine the effectiveness of AI-empowered dignity therapy in enhancing the sense of dignity and reducing depression among older adults.
5. To analyze the supportive role of artificial intelligence within dignity therapy, evaluating both the effectiveness and its practical value in the development of guidelines.

This study employs a mixed-methods research design and will be conducted over a three-year period.

In this study, "AI-empowered " refers to the use of AI technology to assist with data processing. In the first year, an AI system will be developed, followed by a pilot study to evaluate its feasibility and effectiveness.

Participants will receive Dignity Therapy, with assessments of dignity and depression levels conducted immediately upon its completion.

The second year will conduct a randomized controlled trial. Researchers will compare participants who received Dignity Therapy with those who did not, in order to verify the efficacy of AI-enhanced Dignity Therapy in enhancing dignity and reducing depression.

Participants will receive Dignity Therapy, with assessments of dignity and depression levels conducted both immediately after the intervention and three months later.

In the third year, the role of AI within Dignity Therapy will be analyzed. Interviews will be conducted with individuals who completed the Dignity Therapy-as well as their caregivers-to evaluate their experiences and perceptions regarding the use of AI in this context.

Additionally, a random selection of original audio recordings will be reviewed by experts to assess the quality of the transcripts. The study will compare the two versions (AI-assisted vs. standard) in terms of time investment and text quality, using these findings to develop practical guidelines.
interventions: Routine care in Community Integrated Care Centers (C-points) and Daycare Centers
lead_sponsor: Kaohsiung Medical University Chung-Ho Memorial Hospital
title: AI-Empowered Dignity Therapy for the Elderly in Community Integrated Care Centers and Daycare Centers

brief_summary: This study aimed to investigate the acute effects of consuming low glycemic index (LGI) and high glycemic index (HGI) energy bars 60 minutes before exercise on blood glucose levels, heart rate responses, and intermittent endurance performance in amateur soccer players. The study was conducted using a randomized crossover experimental design involving 15 male amateur soccer players aged 18-25 years who regularly participated in soccer training. Each participant completed both experimental conditions, consuming either an LGI or HGI energy bar before exercise, with a 7-day washout period between conditions. Following energy bar consumption, participants performed the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (Yo-Yo IR1) to assess exercise performance. Blood glucose concentrations were measured using capillary blood samples before and after exercise, while heart rate was recorded at rest and immediately following exercise. The study was designed to determine whether the glycemic index of a pre-exercise energy bar influences exercise performance and physiological responses during high-intensity intermittent exercise.

brief_summary:
This study tested whether a one-day Mental Health First Aid course changes how university staff experience their workplace.

Mental Health First Aid is a standard course that teaches people how to notice when someone around them may be struggling with their mental health, how to start a conversation about it, and how to help them reach professional support. It does not train people to act as therapists.

Many university staff work under pressure but find it difficult to say so, because the people who assess their work are often the same people who decide their careers. The researchers wanted to know whether training staff in Mental Health First Aid would change how safe people feel about raising a problem at work, admitting a mistake, or asking a colleague for help. Researchers call this feeling psychological safety.

Eighty-six academic staff at one university in Türkiye took part. Half were chosen at random to attend the eight-hour course, and half joined a waiting list and were offered the same course after the study ended. Everyone completed two questionnaires before the course and again two weeks later: one asking how safe they felt speaking up at work, and one asking what they knew about mental health.

The two groups were then compared to see whether attending the course made a difference.
title: A Vocabulary for Distress: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Mental Health First Aid Training and Perceived Psychological Safety Among Academic Staff

brief_summary:
This study aims to establish a standardized, prospective longitudinal cohort of individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR) to improve early identification, risk prediction, and outcome assessment of psychotic disorders.

The study will recruit individuals at CHR and healthy controls at Shanghai Mental Health Center. Participants will undergo comprehensive assessments covering clinical symptoms, neurocognitive functioning, psychosocial functioning, and multimodal biological characteristics. Assessments will include standardized clinical interviews and rating scales, neurocognitive tests, natural language sampling, eye-tracking, retinal imaging, electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and biological marker assessments, as applicable.

Individuals at CHR will be followed for up to 36 months, with assessments scheduled at baseline and at 2, 6, 12, 24, and 36 months. Healthy controls will undergo assessments at baseline and at 2 months.

The primary outcome is transition to psychosis during follow-up, determined using standardized clinical criteria. Secondary outcomes include changes in clinical symptoms, psychosocial functioning, cognitive performance, and multimodal biological measures.

By integrating longitudinal clinical and multimodal data, this study seeks to identify risk factors and biomarkers associated with psychosis onset and clinical outcomes, and to develop predictive models that may support earlier identification and personalized preventive strategies.

This is an observational study, and no experimental interventions will be assigned as part of the study protocol.
title: Clinical High Risk for Psychosis (CHR) Cohort

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate and compare the clinical efficacy of the Mixed-Thickness Tunnel Access (MiTT) technique versus the Modified Coronally Advanced Tunnel (MCAT) technique, both combined with a subepithelial connective tissue graft (CTG), for the treatment of multiple adjacent Cairo Recession Type 2 (RT2) gingival recession defects.

The study is designed as a two-arm parallel, randomized clinical trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio, enrolling systemically healthy patients with multiple adjacent RT2 recessions. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

Group A (Intervention): Patients treated with the Mixed-Thickness Tunnel Access (MiTT) technique combined with connective tissue graft.

Group B (Control): Patients treated with the Modified Coronally Advanced Tunnel (MCAT) technique combined with connective tissue graft.

The primary objective is to evaluate the reduction in gingival recession depth (GRD) over a 1-year follow-up period. Secondary outcomes include gingival recession width (GRW), percentage of mean root coverage (MRC %), probing pocket depth (PPD), clinical attachment level (CAL), gingival thickness (GT), keratinized tissue width (KTW), postoperative patient satisfaction, postoperative pain, and the root coverage esthetic score (RES).

This study seeks to provide evidence on whether the MiTT technique offers superior or comparable outcomes in managing complex RT2 recession defects.
interventions: Mixed thickness tunnel access with connective tissue graft
Modified Coronally Advanced Tunnel Technique with connective tissue graft
title: Clinical Evaluation of Mixed-Thickness Tunnel Access (MiTT) Versus Modified Coronally Advanced Tunnel (MCAT) With Connective Tissue Graft in Multiple RT2

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to compare the pain-relieving effect of prolotherapy with 5% dextrose and dry needling in adults with local myalgia of the masseter muscle, a type of temporomandibular disorder (TMD). The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* Does prolotherapy with 5% dextrose reduce pain immediately after treatment as much as dry needling?
* How do pain intensity, the number of trigger points and adverse events change at 72 hours and 15 days after each treatment?

Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups and received a single treatment session on the trigger points of the masseter muscles:

* Prolotherapy group: injection of 0.5 mL of 5% dextrose into each trigger point.
* Dry needling group: needling of each trigger point without injecting any substance.

Pain intensity and the number of trigger points were assessed before treatment, immediately after treatment, at 72 hours and at 15 days. Participants were asked to report any adverse event during follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity Immediately After Treatment
title: 5% Dextrose Prolotherapy Versus Dry Needling for Local Myalgia of the Masseter Muscle

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to demonstrate the non-inferiority of the Equinox System with respect to iLux 2020.

Approximately 120 participants are expected to take part in the research trial at a minimum of three (3) and up to five (5) sites across the United States.

The expected duration of the study will be six (6) months, and subject participation will take approximately four (4) weeks, including three (4) visits; pretreatment visit, Treatment Day, two (2) week follow-up and four (4) week follow-up visits.

The investigational therapy in this study is the use of low-level light therapy (LLLT) for the treatment of evaporative dry eye disease due to meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD), when used in conjunction with manual expression of the meibomian glands.

Low-Level Light Therapy (LLLT) is a treatment that uses gentle light to help patient cells work better. The light is applied to the skin using special devices. This light can help repair cells that are damaged and improve the function of healthy cells. It may also warm the natural oils in patient eyelids and could reduce tiny mites that sometimes live near the eyelashes. These effects may support overall eye health and comfort.

Participants will be randomized to receive treatment using the Equinox System (red mask) or iLux 2020 System ("iLux system"). There is a 50% chance participant will receive treatment with the Equinox System (red mask) and 50% chance participant will receive treatment with the iLux 2020 System.

For treatment, participant will be placed in either the prone or supine position. Participant will then wear the red mask for 17 minutes. Special protective eyewear or eye protection is not indicated for this treatment; participant will be instructed to keep eyes closed to ensure full application of the treatment to the upper and lower lids and the periorbital area. Immediately after the treatment is finished, the mask will be removed and the meibomian glands will be manually expressed by a trained and qualified clinician.
primary_outcomes: Equinox System not-inferiority to iLux® System with the respect of change from baseline to Week 4 in Meibomian Gland Score (MGS)
Equinox System not-inferiority to iLux® System with the respect of change from baseline to Week 4 in Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT)
title: Evaluation of the Espansione Equinox System Safety & Effectiveness for the Treatment of Meibomian Gland Dysfunction.

brief_summary:
The Pre-eclampsia Screening Trial to Improve Outcomes (PRESTO) research study aims to assess how clinicians use a blood test to guide care decisions in determining preeclampsia risk, with the overall aim of improving outcomes for both pregnant persons and their babies.

The study will evaluate whether a blood test can help doctors better identify pregnant patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy who are at risk of developing severe pre-eclampsia, which is a serious pregnancy condition that can affect organs such as the liver and kidneys and often leads to preterm delivery. The lab test measures two naturally occurring proteins in the blood that help estimate short-term risk for worsening disease. The goal is to determine whether providing this lab test result to clinicians can improve outcomes including safely prolong pregnancy, reduce unnecessary preterm deliveries, improve newborn outcomes, and optimize hospital care, without increasing complications for pregnant women or causing excess risks to the baby.
title: Preeclampsia Screening Trial to Improve Outcomes

brief_summary: Cerebral palsy (CP) is one of the most common neurodevelopmental disorders worldwide. Although the primary brain lesion is non-progressive, the severity of functional limitations and disability may increase over time due to impairments in muscle tone, balance, postural control, and movement. Furthermore, these impairments may restrict individuals' activity levels and participation in daily life. Various rehabilitation approaches have been described in the literature for individuals with cerebral palsy. Among these, Action Observation Therapy (AOT), which is based on the principles of neuroplasticity and motor learning, is an approach used in neurological rehabilitation. This method involves observing a movement before performing it and has been investigated for improving upper extremity function in individuals with hemiplegia, Parkinson's disease, and cerebral palsy. Dual-task performance refers to the simultaneous execution of a primary task and a secondary task. Performance during dual-task activities may be influenced by several factors, including the nature and difficulty of the tasks, instructions regarding task prioritization, and individual characteristics such as age, cognitive and motor abilities, attentional capacity, and fear of falling. Although studies investigating the use of Action Observation Therapy to improve trunk, upper extremity, and lower extremity functions in children with cerebral palsy are limited, the literature highlights the need to investigate dual-task training in this population. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the effects of dual-task training combined with Action Observation Therapy on body structures and functions, activity, and participation in children diagnosed with hemiplegic cerebral palsy. The findings are expected to contribute to the existing literature and provide further evidence regarding the potential benefits of this combined rehabilitation approach.
interventions: Action Observation Treatment and Dual Task
title: Examination of the Effects of Dual Task Exercise Training Combined With Action Observation Therapy in Children With Spastic Hemiplegic Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
Title: Dietary Habits and Eating Behavior in People with Lipodystrophy: An Observational Study.

Purpose: The purpose of this study is to investigate and analyze the dietary habits and eating behaviors of patients diagnosed with lipodystrophy. Since there is currently a lack of specific data on how these patients approach nutrition, this research aims to provide essential information to improve nutritional guidelines. Additionally, the study seeks to understand if there is a relationship between eating behaviors and the patients' clinical data, such as blood test results and body measurements (anthropometric parameters).

Study Design:

This is an observational, cross-sectional, single-center study with a 2-year enrollment period. Participants will be recruited during their regular medical visits at the Endocrinology Unit of the IRCCS AOU di Bologna, Policlinico Sant'Orsola.

During the study, the following activities will take place:

Clinical Data Collection: Researchers will record body measurements and blood test results as part of standard clinical practice.

Questionnaires: Patients will be asked to complete four specific questionnaires (available in Italian and English) regarding their food frequency, eating behavior patterns, tendencies toward orthorexia, and physical activity levels.

Format: These questionnaires can be completed electronically via a RedCap link (taking approximately 20-30 minutes) or on paper.

Eligibility:

Inclusion Criteria: Adults (18 years or older) with a confirmed diagnosis of lipodystrophy who provide informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria: Patients with HIV-related lipodystrophy or those who cannot understand the languages in which the questionnaires are provided.

Duration and Participation:

The study will last a total of 2 years and 6 months. The first 2 years are dedicated to patient selection and recruitment, followed by 6 months for data analysis. The researchers aim to enroll 30 participants.
primary_outcomes: International Physical Activity Questionnaire - Short Form (IPAQ-Short Form)
title: Eating Habits and Behavior in People Affected by Lipodystrophy: Observational Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to determine whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) clearance at the completion of chemoradiotherapy (chemotherapy and radiation therapy) can predict durable complete response in adults with localized esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). ctDNA clearance refers to the disappearance of detectable tumor DNA from the blood after treatment.

Current methods used to assess treatment response, including imaging scans (PET/CT) and endoscopy, have limitations in reliably identifying patients who achieve a durable complete response after chemoradiotherapy. Researchers will evaluate whether ctDNA clearance improves the prediction of durable complete response beyond standard response assessments. The findings may help identify patients suitable for non-operative management with active surveillance.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Can ctDNA clearance after chemoradiotherapy predict 2-year complete response-disease-free survival?
* Can ctDNA clearance improve the prediction of durable complete response compared with standard response assessment methods, including PET/CT and endoscopy?
* Can ctDNA clearance at different timepoints during and after chemoradiotherapy help identify patients at risk of disease recurrence?

The study will enroll approximately 120 adults with localized esophageal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing curative-intent chemoradiotherapy as part of standard clinical care.

Study participants will:

* Provide blood samples at baseline, during Week 3 of chemoradiotherapy, and at completion of chemoradiotherapy for ctDNA analysis.
* Participate in one of two observational cohorts. Participants in the Longitudinal ctDNA Cohort will provide additional blood samples at 6 weeks and 3 months after chemoradiotherapy and every 3 months through 24 months. Participants in the Limited-Sampling Research Cohort will provide only three protocol-required blood samples.
* Continue standard-of-care cancer treatment and follow-up according to treating physician discretion.
* Allow researchers to review medical records to assess treatment response, cancer recurrence, salvage therapy, and survival status through 24 months after completion of chemoradiotherapy.

Researchers will compare ctDNA results with standard clinical response assessments, including PET/CT and endoscopy, and clinical outcomes. Researchers will also assess whether ctDNA results influence physician treatment recommendations and clinical decision-making in the Longitudinal ctDNA Cohort.

This observational study does not involve investigational therapeutic interventions or require changes to standard clinical management. The findings may help improve risk stratification and identify patients suitable for organ-preservation strategies or closer surveillance following chemoradiotherapy.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving 2-Year Complete Response-Disease-Free Survival (CR-DFS)
title: ctDNA Observational Biomarker Validation Study for Evaluation of Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary:
Study Overview

Title: Effect of cuboid bone manipulation on patients with chronic lateral ankle sprain for volleyball players.

Objective: To examine the impact of cuboid bone manipulation on volleyball players suffering from chronic lateral ankle sprains.

Study Design: A pre-post randomized controlled experimental trial conducted at the Kafr El-Sheikh University outpatient clinic and the Apex center for physical therapy and sports rehabilitation clinic.

Participants and Sample Size

Target Population: 60 volleyball players of both genders, aged 16 to 45 years.

Group Allocation:participants are divided into two equal groups of 30 patients each.

Sample Size Calculation: Estimated using G\*Power software version 3.1.9.2 based on a significance level of $\\alpha = 0.05$, a statistical power of 90%, and an anticipated 10% dropout rate.

Procedures and Methodology

Randomization: A random sequence is generated using online randomization with a 1:1 allocation using random block sizes of four.

Treatment: One group receives a single-session ("one shoot") manipulation of the head of the cuboid bone, while the control group receives no treatment.

Evaluation Measures: Ankle range of motion is measured using an electronic goniometer, ankle pain is measured using a numeric scale, and ankle function is assessed using the ankle joint functional index.

Ethics and Statistical Analysis

Ethical Considerations: Approved by the Research Ethics Committee at Kafr El-Sheikh University in accordance with the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki, featuring voluntary participation, right to withdraw, and mandatory written informed consent.

Statistical Analysis: Data will be analyzed via SPSS software using descriptive statistics, paired t-tests for within-group comparisons, independent t-tests for between-group comparisons, and repeated measures analysis, with statistical significance set at p less than or equal to 0.05.
primary_outcomes: Ankle range of motion measured by an electronic goniometer
title: Effect of Cuboid Bone Manipulation on Patients With Chronic Lateral Ankle Sprain for Volleyball Players

brief_summary: This study aims to address critical gaps in the measurement of health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in children under the age of five by conducting a comprehensive psychometric validation of the EQ-TIPS instrument, including both 3-level and 5-level versions. We will conduct a longitudinal study using both quantitative and qualitative methods to assess the feasibility, face validity, known-groups validity, test-retest reliability, and responsiveness of both EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L in children aged 0-48 months. For children aged 25-48 months, we will also examine the comparability and potential transition between EQ-TIPS-5L and the proxy version of EQ-5D-Y-5L. In addition, we aim to explore spillover effects on family carers by evaluating the psychometric performance, such as known-groups validity, test-retest reliability, and responsiveness of two newly developed EQ-5D-5L bolt-on items (sleep and fatigue) and the EQ-HWB-9. A total of 450 participants will be recruited from three tertiary hospitals in China across three health condition groups: acute illnesses (n=180), chronic conditions (n=180), and healthy controls (n=90), with an approximately balanced distribution across age groups and disease severity levels. The survey questionnaires will include two parts: 1) Child section: EQ-TIPS-3L, EQ-TIPS-5L, proxy EQ VAS, EQ-5D-Y-5L proxy version 1 (only for children aged 25-48 months), a 5-grade overall health assessment (OHA) proxy version, QQ-10 questionnaire, and children's demographic information; 2) Carer section: carers' EQ-5D-5L with sleep and fatigue bolt-ons, carers' EQ VAS, carers' EQ-HWB-9, and carers' demographic information. Each clinical condition is selected for its high prevalence and clinical relevance in early childhood, as well as its suitability for stratifying health status by severity. Additionally, to assess face validity, carers will complete the QQ-10 questionnaire after completing the EQ-TIPS questionnaire to provide structured feedback on the clarity, relevance, and acceptability of EQ-TIPS. Findings will contribute essential evidence to support the use of EQ-TIPS in early childhood HRQoL assessment and of the EQ-5D-5L bolt-ons and EQ-HWB-9 in evaluating caregiver spillover effects. The study data will be shared with the EuroQol Group to support future development and application of these instruments.
interventions: Health-Related Quality of Life Assessment Using EuroQol Instruments
primary_outcomes: Known-Groups Validity of EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L
Test-Retest Reliability of EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L
Responsiveness of EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L to Changes in Child Health
title: A Comprehensive Psychometric Validation of EQ Instruments for Early Childhood Health-Related Quality of Life and Caregiver Spillover

brief_summary: Sensory neuronopathies (SNNs) are rare disorders characterized by damage to sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia. They may have dysimmune, paraneoplastic, toxic, or genetic causes. Alcohol-related nutritional sensory neuronopathy has recently been described and may present acutely or subacutely with pain, mimicking dysimmune or paraneoplastic disease. Distinguishing these causes early may help guide appropriate management. This international, multicentre, retrospective observational cohort study will describe the initial and follow-up clinical and electrophysiological phenotype of acute/subacute alcohol-related nutritional SNN and compare it with dysimmune and paraneoplastic SNN. Data will be abstracted from existing medical records. The protocol anticipates approximately 75 participants with alcohol-related nutritional SNN, 50 with dysimmune SNN, and 20 with paraneoplastic SNN. No additional procedure is performed for research purposes and no direct benefit is expected for participants.
lead_sponsor: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Saint Etienne
title: Phenotype of Alcohol-Related Nutritional Sensory Neuronopathies and Comparison With Dysimmune and Paraneoplastic Forms
