brief_summary: CAROTID STABILISE Pilot tested whether adding alirocumab to high-intensity atorvastatin changes high-risk plaque features in people recently affected by a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) related to carotid artery narrowing. Forty adults aged 40-80 years were randomly assigned in equal groups to alirocumab 150 mg injected under the skin every two weeks or matching placebo every two weeks; both groups took atorvastatin 80 mg daily for 26 weeks. The main outcome was change from baseline to week 26 in intraplaque haemorrhage (IPH) volume measured by high-resolution carotid MRI. Other outcomes included changes in plaque features and LDL cholesterol, safety events, and exploratory recurrent ischemic events or carotid revascularisation. The study was conducted at five sites-four in Egypt and one in Istanbul, Türkiye-and completed on 26 August 2026. This ClinicalTrials.gov record is being submitted retrospectively after study completion; prospective registration on ClinicalTrials.gov is not claimed.
lead_sponsor: Middle East North Africa Stroke and Interventional Neurotherapies Organization
primary_outcomes: Absolute change in carotid intraplaque haemorrhage (IPH) volume
title: CAROTID STABILISE Pilot: Alirocumab for Symptomatic Carotid Stenosis

brief_summary: The goal of this open-label, pilot study, was to evaluate the impact of bowel preparation on IBS patients' gut microbiota, their recovery within thirty days, and whether the probiotic mixture administration contained in Lactichoc® altered their recovery from spontaneous resilience, while simultaneously monitoring the course of gastrointestinal symptoms. The primary objective of our study is to evaluate whether the administration of this probiotics modifies the recovery of the intestinal microbiota after colonoscopy preparation in patients with IBS in terms of speed (kinetics) and extent of recovery, compared to the spontaneous recovery observed in the control group. The secondary objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of probiotics in improving gastrointestinal symptoms and quality of life (GIQLI questionnaire) and stool consistency (Bristol scale), in patients with IBS undergoing colonoscopy, compared to an untreated control group.
title: Probiotic Mixture on Gut Microbiota After Colonscopy in IBS Patients

brief_summary:
This study will test whether adding knife movement training to standard endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) training helps endoscopists perform the procedure faster in a simulation. The added training focuses on how endoscopists move the knife through the endoscope while cutting tissue.

The study plans to enroll 80 endoscopists who have performed 20 to 100 ESD procedures. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group will receive standard ESD training plus knife movement training. The other group will receive standard ESD training alone. Both groups will have one month to practice after training.

Participants will perform ESD on a pig stomach model before training and again after the practice period. The researchers will compare how much dissection speed changes from the first to the second assessment in each group. All study assessments will use the model, with no procedures performed on patients as part of the study.
conditions: Simulation-Based Training in Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in ESD Dissection Speed on an Ex Vivo Porcine Stomach Model
title: Knife Movement Rate Training for Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Randomized Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to compare two different laser settings used to break up kidney and ureter stones during surgery. The study will include adults with kidney or ureter stones who are scheduled to undergo a procedure in which an endoscope is passed through the urinary tract and a laser is used to break the stones into smaller pieces.

The main question is whether one laser setting can break up stones using less energy than the other, while maintaining similar treatment effectiveness and safety.

A total of 110 participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* One group will undergo stone treatment using Moses Technology.
* The other group will undergo stone treatment using Vapor Tunnel.

Both methods use a laser to break stones into smaller pieces. The study will compare the amount of laser energy used in relation to the size of the stone. Researchers will also assess the duration of the procedure, how completely the stones are cleared, the movement of stones during surgery, and any complications.

The findings may help urologists understand which laser setting is more efficient and whether it offers advantages during the treatment of kidney and ureter stones.
lead_sponsor: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
title: Moses Technology vs Vapor Tunnel in Low Power Laser Lithotripsy

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a novel CAR-T cell therapy, called autologous PMCC-COE-HER2FLT3L CAR-T cells, is safe and effective at treating solid tumours that express high levels of the marker HER-2. Patients who have solid tumours that express the marker HER-2, and who have previously progressed or where unsuitable for current HER-2 targeted medications, will be recruited to the study. The PMCC-COE-HER2FLT3L CAR T-cells will be produced using LV and administered to patients after lymphodepleting conditioning chemotherapy. Patients will be then monitored for any side effects as a result of the CAR-T infusion and will have scans performed to assess how their tumour responds to the therapy.
primary_outcomes: Assess the safety of autologous PMCC-COE-HER2FLT3L in patients following lymphodepletion, including identification of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD)
Assess manufacturing feasibility of PMCC-COE-HER2FLT3L, defined as the percentage of patients in whom a suitable product manufactured, meeting pre-determined criteria for release.
title: Evaluation of FLT3L Armoured CAR T-cells in HER2 Expressing Malignant Diseases in Adults

brief_summary: Study aims to assess the quality of life and mental health of patients suffering from infertility. Secondly, this study aims to discover the true reasons for choosing a certain IVF treatment (whether quality of life related or otherwise) and the extent to which defined factors (e.g. cost, doctor recommendations, stress levels and effectiveness) influence this choice. Thirdly, the study aims to examine psychological resilience in adhering to a treatment choice and the reasons for changing treatment. Finally, we will evaluate the cumulative live birth rate over a planned timeframe, including that experienced with IVF Naturelle, as these are currently unknown.
title: Quality of Life, Decision-making, Resilience, Satisfaction and Success Rate of Different IVF Treatment Strategies: an International Prospective Cohort Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether remote follow-up can work as well as regular in-person follow-up at the hospital for young adults with inflammatory joint diseases who have low disease activity. The study includes people aged 18 to 30 years with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, or spondyloarthritis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is remote follow-up non-inferior (not worse than) to regular in-person follow-up at the hospital in keeping participants' disease under good control over 24 months?
* Is remote follow-up non-inferior to regular in-person follow-up when it comes to disease flare-ups, use of healthcare services, medication use, satisfaction with care, and safety? Researchers will compare a remote follow-up program, with fewer routine outpatient visits, to regular in-person follow-up to see whether disease control after 24 month is non-inferior (not worse)

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either remote digital follow-up or regular in-person follow-up at the hospital .
* Complete questionnaires about their symptoms, health, and treatment during the study.
* Attend appointments with a rheumatologist at the start of the study and at study end at 24 months.
* If assigned to remote follow-up, complete questionnaires every 3 months using a smartphone or tablet application and communicate with a study nurse when needed through secure messaging in the remote monitoring software platform.
* If assigned to regular in-person follow-up, attend routine appointments at the rheumatology clinic according to usual practice.

This study aims to determine whether remote follow-up can provide a safe and effective alternative to regular in-person follow-up for young adults with inflammatory joint diseases who have low disease activity .
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants in low disease activity
title: Remote Monitoring in Young Adults With Inflammatory Joint Disease

brief_summary:
This is a 3-arm, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel, controlled, non-inferiority study comparing DLBS3233 at a dose of 100 mg once daily; DLBS3233 at a dose of 200 mg once daily; and Metformin XR 500 mg twice daily for a 12-week course of therapy.

DLBS3233 is a bioactive fraction derived from a combination of Lagerstroemia speciosa and Cinnamomum burmanii. DLBS3233 exhibits antidiabetic properties by enhancing insulin signaling, improving glucose uptake, modulating lipid metabolism, and reducing insulin resistance.
title: The Efficacy and Safety of DLBS3233 in Adults With Prediabetes

brief_summary:
This trial is a phase I trial in patients with metastasized castration resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) after failure of at least third-line therapy aiming to evaluate safety and efficacy of CC-1, a bispecific antibody (bsAb) with PSMAxCD3 specificity. CC-1 binds to human prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) on prostate cancer cells as well as to tumor vessels of CRPC, thereby allowing for a dual mode of anti-cancer action. CC-1 was developed in a novel format which not only prolongs serum half-life but most importantly reduces off-target T cell activation with expected fewer side effects. Together with pre-emptive IL-6 receptor (IL-6R) blockade using tocilizumab, this allows for application of effective bsAb doses with expected high anticancer activity. The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of once per week subcutaneously (SC) applied CC-1 has been established in the DKTK\_PMO\_1605 trial. This is a phase Ib trial to further explore the efficacy and safety of the MTD of SC CC-1.

A translational research program comprising, among others, analysis of CC-1 half-life and molecular profiling in liquid biopsies will serve to better define the mode of action of CC-1 and to identify biomarkers for further clinical development.
title: Bispecific PSMAxCD3 Antibody CC-1 Applied Subcutaneously in Patients With Castration Resistant Prostate Carcinoma

brief_summary: In this research study, we will be evaluating whether an anesthesia provider using the method of intravenous lidocaine infusion during the perioperative and immediate postoperative period can provide equal short-term pain control and decrease postoperative opioid consumption compared to traditional opioid utilization. We will also evaluate the effects of intravenous lidocaine on inflammatory mediators such as interleukins and cytokines through timed lab draws. The study hypothesis is that intravenous lidocaine will provide similar pain relief and decrease the amount of post operative opioids used, as well as decrease the amount of inflammatory mediators present compared to conventional post-operative treatment utilizing solely opioids.
title: IV Lidocaine in Ortho Trauma Patients

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human, phase I clinical study aimed at evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and preliminary antitumor efficacy of AK158D1 in advanced solid tumors.
title: A Study of AK158D1 in Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary: This study is a Phase I, single-dose, open-label trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of a single dose of SYH2053 injection in participants with moderate, and severe renal impairment compared to participants with normal renal function.
primary_outcomes: Area under the curve of the plasma concentration (AUC)
Time to reach maximum plasma concentration (Tmax)
Amount excreted unchanged in urine (Ae) of SYH2053 over 72 hours post-dose
Fraction excreted (fe) of SYH2053 over 72 hours post-dose
The serum Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level
title: A Study of SYH2053 Injection in Participants With Renal Impairment Compared to Participants With Normal Renal Function

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare two positions used for whole-breast radiation therapy in Thai women who have undergone breast-conserving surgery: lying on the back (supine) and lying face down (prone).

Radiation therapy after breast-conserving surgery helps reduce the risk of breast cancer returning. However, some radiation may reach nearby organs, particularly the heart and lungs. The position used during treatment may affect how much radiation these organs receive.

In this study, 24 women will undergo radiation treatment planning CT scans in both the supine and prone positions. Researchers will create a radiation treatment plan for each position and compare how well the plans cover the breast while minimizing radiation exposure to the heart and lungs. Each participant will receive actual radiation treatment in only one of the two positions, selected based on treatment planning results and clinical suitability.

The study will also assess patient comfort, positioning accuracy, treatment setup time, and treatment-related side effects.

The findings may help identify which patients are more likely to benefit from prone positioning and support individualized breast radiation treatment planning in Thai women.
primary_outcomes: Mean Heart Dose in Supine Versus Prone Treatment Plans
Mean Ipsilateral Lung Dose in Supine Versus Prone Treatment Plans
title: Supine Versus Prone Whole-Breast Radiotherapy in Thai Women After Breast-Conserving Surgery

brief_summary: Evaluate the safety and tolerability of stereotactic injection of KL002 into the putamen of patients with advanced primary PD.
interventions: Injecting KL002 into the bilateral putamen
primary_outcomes: The incidence rate of DLT events
title: Gene Therapy of Parkinson's Disease With KL002 in a Phase 1/2a Clinical Study

brief_summary: This randomised controlled trial aimed to evaluate the effects of flipped learning-based postoperative patient education on knowledge level and knowledge retention, post-discharge care adherence, satisfaction with education, perceived readiness for discharge, and care dependency in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The intervention group received flipped learning-based postoperative patient education incorporating an educational booklet, videos, and face-to-face reinforcement, whereas the control group received conventional postoperative patient education. Knowledge was assessed before education, immediately after education, and on the seventh day after discharge. The study was conducted at the General Surgery Ward of Zonguldak Atatürk State Hospital.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Knowledge Level and Knowledge Retention
title: Flipped Learning-Based Postoperative Patient Education in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Randomised Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine the effects of a clinical treatment called deep brain reorienting (DBR) on post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

We will be investigating if DBR helps reduce PTSD symptoms. To do so, we will be assigning participants to either receive DBR or continue with their current treatment. By comparing the results from the two groups, we will learn if DBR could be an effective treatment for PTSD.

Participants will be randomly assigned (e.g., like the flip of a coin) to receive either eight weekly sessions of DBR treatment or continue with their current treatment. Participants assigned to continue with their current treatment will be offered eight DBR sessions after they have completed the study.

The study will take place online/virtually over video conferencing.
lead_sponsor: The Royal Ottawa Mental Health Centre
primary_outcomes: Change in clinician-assessed PTSD symptoms from baseline as measured by the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale-5 (CAPS-5) at the post-treatment assessment.
Change in clinician-assessed PTSD symptoms from baseline as measured by the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale-5 (CAPS-5) at the three-month follow-up assessment.
Change in self-reported PTSD symptoms from baseline as measured by the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) at the post-treatment assessment.
Change in self-reported PTSD symptoms from baseline as measured by the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) at the three-month follow-up assessment.
title: Deep Brain Reorienting (DBR) in Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)

brief_summary: This single-center cross-sectional study aims to determine the prevalence of erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation in sexually active men aged 18 to 40 years and to evaluate their association with depressive and anxiety symptoms, lifestyle factors, and sociodemographic characteristics. Participants attending outpatient clinics of Ondokuz Mayis University Hospital for routine health check-ups completed a structured questionnaire, the International Index of Erectile Function-15 (IIEF-15), the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool (PEDT), the Beck Depression Inventory, and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale.
title: Sexual Dysfunction in Young Adult Men

brief_summary:
This is a multicentre, international, non-profit observational study aimed at prospectively validating a personalized diagnostic and therapeutic algorithm based on the Dejour v3.0 classification in patients with recurrent objective patellar instability and trochlear dysplasia.

The primary objective is to compare treatment failure rates at 24 months between patients with severe trochlear dysplasia (trochlear bump \>5 mm) treated with trochleoplasty and MPFL reconstruction, and a retrospective control group with similar trochlear morphology treated without trochleoplasty.

Secondary outcomes include clinical and functional outcomes assessed using validated scores (IKDC, Kujala, Tegner and BPII 2.0), cartilage status assessed by MRI using the MOAKS score, and postoperative complications, particularly arthrofibrosis.

Patients aged 14-49 years will be enrolled at IRCCS Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli and Lyon Ortho Clinic. The study includes both a prospective cohort managed according to the Dejour v3.0 algorithm and a retrospective historical control cohort. Follow-up assessments will be performed up to 24 months after surgery.

The study is planned to start on October 1, 2026, with an expected completion date of September 30, 2029. A total sample size of 152 patients (76 per group) is planned.
title: Trochleoplasty in the Management of Objective Patellar Instability: a Personalized Surgical Approach for the Prevention of Recurrence in Patients With Trochlear Dysplasia

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the acute effects of green tea intake on countermovement jump performance and cognitive performance in male Taekwondo athletes. A randomized, placebo-controlled, three-condition crossover design will be used. Each participant will complete control, placebo, and green tea conditions in a randomized and counterbalanced order, with a washout period of at least 72 hours between sessions. CMJ performance will be assessed as the primary outcome, followed by the Stroop test as the secondary outcome.
title: Acute Effects of Green Tea Intake on Countermovement Jump and Cognitive Performance in Taekwondo Athletes

brief_summary:
Inappropriate antimicrobial prescribing is common in hospitalised patients and is associated with worse outcomes. Clinical pharmacists are core members of antimicrobial stewardship teams, but the evidence comes almost entirely from intensive care units and from undifferentiated hospital-wide analyses.

This trial tested whether adding pharmacist-led antimicrobial therapy optimization to standard care improves the quality of antibiotic prescribing in an intermediate care unit, a setting where antimicrobial therapy is often the main therapeutic intervention.

Adults admitted with an active infection and antibiotics started within the previous 72 hours were randomly assigned to standard care or to standard care plus a structured daily pharmacist review of five prescribing domains during the first four days. The primary outcome was optimal prescribing at day 4, defined as meeting all five domains simultaneously.
title: Pharmacist-Led Antimicrobial Therapy Optimization in Intermediate Care

brief_summary:
Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is characterized by a reduction in the number and/or quality of remaining oocytes and may affect women's reproductive health. Antarctic krill oil contains omega-3 fatty acids, phospholipids, and other bioactive components. However, its potential effects on ovarian reserve in women with DOR remain unclear.

This study aims to evaluate the effects and safety of Antarctic krill oil supplementation in women with diminished ovarian reserve.

This is a prospective, single-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group controlled trial conducted at Qilu Hospital of Shandong University, China. A total of 158 women with DOR, aged 30 to 40 years, are planned to be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either Antarctic krill oil or an olive oil control for 12 weeks.

The primary outcome is the change in bilateral antral follicle count (AFC) from baseline to 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes include changes in serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), estradiol (E2), and measures of menopausal symptoms, sleep quality, anxiety, depression, and osteoporosis risk. Safety will be assessed through adverse event monitoring and relevant laboratory examinations.

This study is expected to provide clinical evidence regarding the potential effects and safety of Antarctic krill oil supplementation in women with diminished ovarian reserve.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) Levels
title: Effects of Antarctic Krill Oil on Ovarian Reserve in Women With Diminished Ovarian Reserve

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of individualized intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) on depressive and gastrointestinal symptoms in patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and depressive symptoms.

A total of 60 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to active or sham stimulation. Individualized stimulation targets within the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) will be identified using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).

Participants will receive 10 stimulation sessions over two weeks. Clinical assessments and multimodal brain MRI will be performed at baseline and at the end of Week 2. The primary outcome will be the change in depressive symptom severity measured by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17).

An optional ancillary study involving paired stool sample collection at baseline and Week 2 is planned to support future exploratory investigations of gut microbiota and its associations with clinical symptoms and brain network characteristics. This ancillary component will be implemented only after the relevant ethics approval and additional informed consent have been obtained.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Hangzhou Normal University
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Depressive Symptom Severity Assessed by HAMD-17 at Week 2
title: Individualized Brain Stimulation for Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Depressive Symptoms

brief_summary:
Rationale Patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), a sudden medical emergency where blood flow to the heart is blocked, require dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 12 months to prevent dangerous blood clots to form. This typically includes the combination of aspirin and a form of P2Y12 inhibitor, a specific type of medicine that stops platelet cells to clot. Irrespective of the treatment strategy (i.e., invasive through angioplasty or conservative with medication only), the somewhat more potent P2Y12 inhibitor ticagrelor is advised over clopidogrel. Yet, clopidogrel can be considered for patients with a higher bleeding risk, as it is associated with fewer bleeding events.

Although ischemic complications (problems that happen when the heart doesn't get enough blood and oxygen) usually appear in the first 30 days after ACS diagnosis, the bleeding risks remains high through the entire period of DAPT. A de-escalation strategy (switch from ticagrelor to clopidogrel after 30 days) could theoretically reduce the number of bleeding events, without increasing the number of ischemic events. However, in 30% of the (white) European patients, there is a small change (mutation) in their genetic material. They are carriers of at least one so called CYP2C19 loss-of-function (LOF) allele, which results in a poor or intermediate processing of clopidogrel in to its active form.

Despite knowledge of these loss of function mutations, current treatment guidelines for ACS do not provide specific recommendations on individualized, genotype-based treatment (i.e. using the unique genetic code to choose the medicine that works best) with P2Y12 inhibitors. In addition, previous conducted trials on a de-escalation strategy have not led to strong recommendations, as they were too small and cautious to give definite answers.

Objective The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether individualized genotype-guided treatment with DAPT after ACS diagnosis is just as safe and effective as standard clinical practice.

Participants will receive:

1. Standard treatment at the discretion of the cardiologist, or
2. Genotype-guided treatment (based on the presence of a LOF allele)

Participants included in the genotype-guided group who do not carry a LOF allele will be classified as normal processors of clopidogrel, and will de-escalate after 30 days from standard therapy to clopidogrel. If patients are proven carriers of one of the LOF alleles, de-escalation will not take place and treatment will continue as previously started.

Participants will be followed for 18 months after ACS diagnosis to collect medical data and to complete questionnaires.
title: Individualized Genotype-guided Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome

brief_summary:
This is a single-arm, phase II clinical study. A total of 43 treatment-naive hepatocellular carcinoma patients with portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) are planned to be enrolled. Eligible subjects will enter the study after signing informed consent.

Each subject will receive TAE-HAIC combined with Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab (QL1706, 7.5 mg/kg, iv, Q3W) and lenvatinib (8 mg for body weight \<60 kg, or 12 mg for body weight \>60 kg, po, QD). QL1706 is administered on Day 2 of interventional therapy, with a 21-day cycle. Lenvatinib is taken orally on the day of discharge after QL1706 infusion. The HAIC cycles will be determined by investigators according to the subject's condition, ranging from 3 to 6 cycles.

QL1706 and lenvatinib can be maintained for up to 2 years, until disease progression (PD, comprehensively assessed by investigators based on imaging and clinical status), loss of clinical benefit, intolerable toxicity, withdrawal of informed consent, initiation of new anti-tumor therapy, or other treatment discontinuation criteria specified in the protocol, whichever occurs first. For subjects withdrawn due to PD, subsequent treatment options may include targeted agents (apatinib, regorafenib, ramucirumab), immunotherapy (pembrolizumab, camrelizumab, tislelizumab), traditional Chinese medicine preparations with indications for hepatocellular carcinoma, best supportive care or palliative care, in accordance with the 2025 CSCO or NCCN guidelines, at the investigator's discretion.

Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI (PET-CT when necessary) will be performed every 6 weeks (±7 days) from treatment initiation for efficacy assessment until PD, death, intolerable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, initiation of new anti-tumor therapy or other protocol-specified discontinuation reasons, whichever comes first. Subjects will continue safety visits and survival follow-up after treatment discontinuation. Safety follow-up lasts for 30 days after the last dose (90 days for immune-related adverse events). Survival follow-up is conducted every 3 months within 2 years and every 6 months thereafter up to 3 years after treatment discontinuation or death. For subjects stopping treatment for reasons other than PD or death, tumor progression follow-up including serum tumor markers (AFP, PIVKA-II (DCP)) and imaging examinations (dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI/CT of abdomen and pelvis) will be arranged.

TAE: particulate embolic agents such as gelatin sponge particles, blank microspheres and PVA particles are used to embolize tumor feeding arteries.

HAIC-FOLFOX regimen: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² intra-arterial infusion over 2-3 h, leucovorin 400 mg/m² intra-arterial infusion over 1-2 h, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² intra-arterial bolus followed by continuous intra-arterial infusion of 2400 mg/m² for 23 h or 46 h, repeated every 3 weeks.
title: A Single-Arm, Exploratory, Phase II Study of Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab Combined With Local Therapy as First-Line Treatment for Hepatocellular Carcinoma With Portal Vein Tumor Thrombus

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether tele-nursing (education and follow-up provided by a nurse by telephone) after hospital discharge improves adherence, self-confidence and quality of life in patients who perform clean intermittent catheterization (CIC).

Clean intermittent catheterization is a method of emptying the bladder at regular intervals with a catheter in people who cannot empty their bladder on their own, such as people with spinal cord injury. After discharge, patients may have difficulty performing catheterization correctly and regularly, which can lead to complications and reduce their quality of life.

Adult patients performing CIC who were about to be discharged from a spinal cord injury rehabilitation clinic in Ankara, Türkiye, were included in the study. All patients received the clinic's routine discharge education. In addition, patients in the intervention group received 10 structured telephone sessions with a nurse during the 8 weeks after discharge. The control group received routine education only. Adherence to catheterization, self-confidence in performing catheterization and catheterization-related quality of life were measured before discharge and 8 weeks after discharge.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Who Found the Tele-Nursing Program Useful
title: Effect of Tele-Nursing on Adherence, Self-Confidence and Quality of Life in Patients Using Clean Intermittent Catheterization

brief_summary:
The aim of this pilot study is to assess the effects of 10 weeks of omega-3 fatty acid supplementation on selected motor performance parameters, bone turnover markers, regulators of bone remodeling, and bone mineral density in female soccer players and women with low levels of physical activity. Changes in the erythrocyte omega-3 fatty acid profile, including EPA and DHA levels and the Omega-3 Index, will also be assessed, along with potential differences in response to supplementation between the two populations.

This will be an interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. A total of 40 women aged 18-35 years will be enrolled: 20 female soccer players and 20 women with low levels of physical activity. Within each population, participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to the omega-3 supplementation or placebo group, yielding four parallel study groups. Over 10 weeks, participants assigned to omega-3 will take three capsules daily providing 1,677 mg of EPA and 687 mg of DHA. Participants assigned to placebo will take three capsules daily providing a total of 3,000 mg of MCT oil.

Assessments will be performed at three time points: T0 (baseline, before the start of supplementation), T1 (after 5 weeks of supplementation), and T2 (after 10 weeks of supplementation). Assessments will include handgrip strength, back muscle strength, lower-limb power assessed by vertical jump testing, bone turnover markers and regulators of bone remodeling, body composition and bone mineral density measured by DXA, the erythrocyte fatty acid profile, selected hormonal parameters, and dietary intake.

The effects of supplementation will be evaluated by assessing changes in the measured parameters at weeks 5 and 10 relative to baseline (T0). The magnitude of these changes will also be compared between the omega-3 and placebo groups, taking participants' level of physical activity into account.
lead_sponsor: Wroclaw University of Health and Sport Sciences
title: Effects of Omega-3 Supplementation on Motor Performance and Bone Turnover Markers in Women: A Pilot Study

brief_summary: This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of therapeutic play on fear and anxiety levels in children before ultrasound examinations. This controlled pretest-posttest study was conducted in the pediatric clinic of a city hospital between September 2025 and February 2026. The study was completed with 60 children aged 6-12 years (study group = 30, control group = 30). Data were collected using the Demographic Information Form, Children's Fear Scale, and Children's Anxiety Scale-State Anxiety. The study group received therapeutic play using handmade amigurumi materials before the ultrasound examination, while the control group received routine care.
title: The Effects of Therapeutic Play on Fear and Anxiety Before Ultrasound Examinations in Children Aged 6-12

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a six-month clinical pharmacist-led pharmaceutical care intervention on medication adherence, beliefs about medicines, and health-related quality of life in adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) receiving antidepressant treatment.

A total of 186 participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either structured pharmaceutical care in addition to usual psychiatric care or usual psychiatric care alone. Of these, 170 participants completed the six-month follow-up.

The intervention included individualized patient counseling, medication review, identification and management of medication-related problems, and telephone follow-up every two weeks.

Medication adherence was assessed using the Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5), beliefs about medicines using the Turkish Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire (BMQ-T), and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D-3L and EQ-VAS. Assessments were conducted at baseline, Month 3, and Month 6.
primary_outcomes: Change in Medication Adherence as Measured by MARS-5
title: Effect of Clinical Pharmacist-Led Pharmaceutical Care in Major Depressive Disorder

brief_summary:
This study aims to develop and validate the AI-Integrated Motor Assessment System (AIMAS) for evaluating motor skills in children aged 6 to 12 years. The study will include typically developing children and children with developmental delay or motor-related developmental disorders.

Participants will complete standardized gross and fine motor tasks while their movements are video-recorded for AI-based analysis. Some participants will also complete a standardized clinical motor assessment for comparison.

The study will evaluate the reliability, validity, and accuracy of AIMAS, including its ability to identify children with motor difficulties. The long-term goal is to establish AIMAS as an accessible and efficient screening tool that can support earlier referral for further professional assessment.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy of AIMAS for Identifying Motor Developmental Difficulties
title: Development and Validation of an AI-Driven Motor Skill Assessment System for Children

brief_summary: Chronic cervicalgia (chronic neck pain) is one of the most prevalent musculoskeletal disorders worldwide and is associated with pain, reduced cervical mobility, functional limitations, poor posture, and decreased quality of life. It commonly develops due to prolonged poor posture, excessive use of electronic devices, sedentary lifestyle, and repetitive strain on cervical structures. Physiotherapy interventions play a vital role in the conservative management of chronic neck pain, with exercise-based approaches being widely used to reduce symptoms and restore functional abilities. Among these interventions, the McKenzie Method and Dynamic Neck Exercises are commonly applied in clinical practice; however, limited evidence exists regarding their comparative effectiveness in managing chronic cervicalgia. Therefore, the objective of this randomized clinical trial is to compare the effects of the McKenzie Method and Dynamic Neck Exercises on pain intensity, cervical range of motion, and neck disability in patients with chronic cervicalgia. A total of 36 participants aged between 18-40 years with chronic neck pain will be recruited and randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive McKenzie neck exercises focusing on repeated directional movements and postural correction, while Group B will receive Dynamic Neck Exercises using controlled cervical movements and resistance-based training. Both groups will additionally receive hot pack therapy for 15 minutes prior to intervention as a baseline treatment. The treatment protocol will consist of three sessions per week for four weeks, making a total of 12 treatment sessions. Outcome measures including pain intensity, cervical range of motion, and neck-related disability will be assessed using the Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS),Digital Goniometer, and Neck Disability Index (NDI) at baseline and after the fourth week of intervention. The collected data will be statistically analysed using SPSS version 24 to determine the comparative effectiveness of both treatment approaches. This study is expected to provide evidence-based guidance for physiotherapists in selecting the most effective rehabilitation approach for improving pain, mobility, and functional outcomes in individuals with chronic cervicalgia.

brief_summary:
This single-center, observational, analytical, ambispective study aims to develop and internally validate a clinical decision support system for cataract surgery planning using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) integrated into the ARGOS optical biometer.

The study will evaluate the ability of preoperative crystalline lens tomographic patterns (Types I-III) to predict surgical complexity and the surgical approach required during cataract extraction. Additionally, it will assess whether SS-OCT-derived information provides incremental predictive value beyond conventional clinical assessment using the Lens Opacities Classification System III (LOCS III).

Clinical, biometric, and surgical data will be analyzed to determine the predictive performance, reproducibility, and technical feasibility of the proposed classification system. The ultimate goal is to establish an objective, noninvasive, and reproducible tool to support personalized surgical planning and preoperative risk stratification in cataract surgery.

brief_summary: This prospective randomized controlled study will compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy and opioid-sparing effect of ultrasound-guided bilateral intertransverse process block (ITPB) with bilateral transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block combined with rectus sheath block in adults undergoing elective robotic or laparoscopic hepatectomy. A total of 64 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the ITPB group or the TAP block group. Both groups will receive standardized general anesthesia and multimodal postoperative analgesia, including patient-controlled analgesia. The primary outcome is cumulative opioid consumption during the first 24 hours after surgery, expressed as intravenous morphine equivalents. Secondary outcomes include cumulative opioid consumption through 72 hours, incisional and visceral pain intensity, shoulder pain, sensory block distribution, rescue analgesic use, quality of recovery, postoperative recovery parameters, and adverse events.

brief_summary:
Coronary heart disease causes narrowing of the heart (coronary) arteries (arteries are blood vessels, which supply oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle). Your heart specialist will have explained to you that they suspect that you have a narrowing in one or more of your heart arteries. This narrowing may be causing you to have chest pains or evidence of reduced blood supply to your heart muscle.

One commonly used treatment for this problem is to stretch the narrowing with a balloon and then insert a small mesh-like device called a stent, which will hold the artery open, improving the blood flow to your heart, and thereby help with your symptoms. An alternative treatment is to open the narrowing with a balloon that is coated with an anti-inflammatory drug (so called drug-coated balloon) as treatment instead of a stent. Drug-coated balloons are used to reduce the risk of re-narrowing of your coronary arteries without leaving an implant (like a stent) behind. A stent (which is a foreign object that does not belong in the body) can cause vessel inflammation and it bears the risk of blockage within the stent (in-stent restenosis or ISR). Drug-coated balloons leave no implant behind but target the narrowing in your vessel wall with the delivery of an anti-inflammatory agent to the vessel wall, allowing the blood vessel to heal.

Biosensors has developed a balloon coated with a drug called Biolimus A9™ which suppresses inflammation in the artery where the narrowing has occurred. We refer to this balloon coated with Biolimus A9™ as BA9-DCB (Biolimus A9™ drug-coated balloon) also known as BioRISE. This device is not commercially available and will be tested in this study for the first time in humans. However, several coronary stents made by Biosensors are already on the market that contain the Biolimus A9™ drug. It has been proven to be safe and effective in preventing re-narrowing of the artery where the stent is placed.

In this study, two types of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) will be used; the BioRISE (test group; group 1) and SELUTION SLR, a balloon that is coated with sirolimus (control group; group 2). The SELUTION SLR balloon is commercially available in Europe.

The study has the following design:

• Patients will be treated according to standard hospital procedures using the study device.

The study has the following design:

* Patients will be treated according to standard hospital procedures using the study device.
* There will be two different types of patients included in this study.
* 400 patients with a narrowing in a heart artery that has never been treated before (referred to as de novo disease), of whom 200 will be treated with the BioRISE balloon and 200 with the SELUTION SLR balloon. The allocation to the two possible treatments is random as it must be in a study like this. Of these 400 patients, 15 in each treatment arm, will have the inside of the artery imaged during the procedure using a well-established technique called Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) and Quantitative Flow Ratio (QFR)
* 43 patients with a narrowing inside a stent that was implanted in the past (referred to as in-stent restenosis). In these patients, only the BioRISE balloon will be used.
* Your doctor will explain to which category applies to you.
* There will be up to 25 hospitals taking part in the study in the UK, and in up to 5 European countries
* Patients will be taking part in the study for up to 3 years, and during this time their health status will be assessed by telephone or hospital visit at 1month, 9 month, 12 months, 24 months and 36 months.
* There will be a check up angiography to assess the primary end point at 9 months for all participants.
primary_outcomes: In-segment Late Lumen Loss (LLL) at 9 months
title: Study of the BioRISE Biolimus Drug-Coated Balloon Versus the SELUTION SLR Sirolimus-Coated Balloon in De Novo Coronary Lesions, With a Single-Arm In-Stent Restenosis Cohort (SUNRISE)

brief_summary: This randomised controlled trial investigated the effect of skin antisepsis performed with povidone-iodine warmed to 36°C, compared with room-temperature povidone-iodine, on perioperative comfort, pain intensity, and physiological parameters in patients aged 65 years and older undergoing elective coronary angiography. The study was conducted at the Coronary Angiography Unit of Zonguldak Atatürk State Hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to either the intervention group (warmed povidone-iodine at 36°C) or the control group (room-temperature povidone-iodine). Perioperative comfort was assessed using the Perioperative Comfort Questionnaire, pain intensity was measured using a Visual Analogue Scale, and physiological parameters including systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, body temperature, and peripheral oxygen saturation were recorded at four time points: before antisepsis, immediately after antisepsis, after local anaesthetic injection, and after vascular access.
title: Warmed Povidone-Iodine Skin Antisepsis and Perioperative Comfort in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: A Randomised Controlled Trial
